scenario: The washing machine does not start even when the door is closed and the Start/Pause button is pressed.
solution_steps:
1. Make sure the washing machine is plugged in.
2. Make sure the door is properly closed.
3. Make sure the water taps are open.
4. Make sure to press or tap Start/Pause to start the washing machine.
5. Make sure Child Lock is not activated.
6. Check the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.
7. Before the washing machine starts to fill, it will make a series of clicking noises to check the door lock and does a quick drain.

scenario: The washing machine's Child Lock feature is activated and prevents operation.
solution_steps:
1. To release the Child Lock function, hold down Temp. and Spin simultaneously for 3 seconds.
2. NOTE: In the Child Lock state, you must first release the Child Lock if you want to add detergent or laundry.
3. Your setting will be kept even after restarting the machine.

scenario: Detergent remains in the detergent drawer after the wash cycle is complete.
solution_steps:
1. While holding down the release lever (A) on the inner of the drawer, slide open the drawer.
2. Remove the release lever and the liquid detergent guide from the drawer.
3. Clean the drawer components in flowing water using a soft brush.
4. Clean the drawer recess using a bottle brush to remove detergent residues and limescale on the drawer recess.
5. Reinsert the release lever and the liquid detergent guide to the drawer.
6. Slide the drawer inward to close it.
7. To remove remaining detergent, perform the RINSE+SPIN cycle with the drum being empty.

scenario: The water supply hose is kinked or clogged, preventing proper water flow.
solution_steps:
1. Turn off the washing machine, and unplug the power cord.
2. Close the water tap.
3. Loosen and disconnect the water hose from the back of the washing machine. Cover the hose with a cloth to prevent water from gushing out.
4. Use pliers to pull out the mesh filter from the inlet valve.
5. Submerge the mesh filter deeply in water so that the threaded connector is also submerged.
6. Dry the mesh filter completely in the shade.
7. Reinsert the mesh filter into the inlet valve, and reconnect the water hose to the inlet valve.
8. Open the water tap and check if there are any leaks around the connection areas. If there are water leaks, repeat the steps above.
9. Make sure the water taps are open.
10. Make sure that the cold water tap and the hot water tap are properly connected.
11. Make sure the washing machine is running with sufficient water pressure.
12. If the mesh filter is clogged, an information code of “4C” appears on the screen. 

(Note: Steps 9-12 are from the troubleshooting advice provided for the "4C" information code, which indicates that water is not supplied properly.)

scenario: The filter is clogged, affecting the appliance's performance.
solution_steps:
1. Turn off the Laundry Combo, and then unplug the power cord.
2. Close the water tap.
3. Loosen and disconnect the water hose from the back of the Laundry Combo. Cover the end of each hose with a cloth or towel to prevent water from gushing out.
4. Use pliers to pull out the mesh filter from the inlet valve.
5. Submerge the mesh filter deeply in water so that the threaded connector is also submerged.
6. Dry the mesh filter completely in the shade.
7. Reinsert the mesh filter into the inlet valve, and reconnect the water hose to the inlet valve.
8. Open the water tap.

scenario: The washing machine does not start despite pressing the start button.

6. Before the washing machine starts to fill, it will make a series of clicking noises to check the door lock and will do quick drain.
7. Check the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.
8. Check if power is supplied properly.
9. Low voltage detected. Check if the power cord is plugged in.
10. Make sure laundry is not caught in the door.

solution_steps:

scenario: The Smart Diagnosis function does not operate due to Wi-Fi unavailability or disconnection.
solution_steps:
1. If the appliance cannot be connected due to problems with the wireless signal transmission, unplug the appliance and wait about a minute before trying again.

2. The network connection may not work properly depending on the Internet service provider.

3. The Wi-Fi may not connect or the connection may be interrupted because of the home network environment.

4. If the firewall on your wireless router is enabled, disable the firewall or add an exception to it.

5. The wireless network name (SSID) should be a combination of English letters and numbers. (Do not use special characters.)

6. If the security protocol of the router is set to WEP, network setup may fail. Change the security protocol (WPA2 is recommended), and connect the product again.

7. Only a 2.4 GHz router frequency is supported. Set the wireless router to 2.4 GHz and connect the appliance to the wireless router. To check the router frequency, check with your Internet service provider or the router manufacturer.

scenario: The appliance does not operate properly if the water inlet hose is frozen and not defrosted before use.
solution_steps:
1 Turn off the washer, and unplug the power cord.
2 Turn off the faucets connected to the water inlet hoses.
3 Pour hot water on the frozen faucets to thaw the water inlet hoses and remove the water inlet hoses.
4 Immerse the water inlet hoses in hot water to thaw them.
5 Reconnect the water inlet hoses to the water inlets of the washer and to the faucets. See Connecting the Water Inlet Hoses for details.
6 Turn on the faucets.
7 Press the Power button to turn on the washer.
8 Select the Spin cycle to operate spin only cycle for draining and spinning.
9 Press the Start/Pause button.

scenario: The Smart DiagnosisTM feature does not function due to Wi-Fi disconnection or app unavailability.
solution_steps:

2. If you experience a problem with your Wi-Fi equipped appliance, it can transmit troubleshooting data to a smartphone using the LG ThinQ application.
3. Launch the LG ThinQ application and select the Smart DiagnosisTM feature in the menu.
4. Follow the instructions provided in the LG ThinQ application.
5. Ensure the password for the Wi-Fi network was entered correctly.
6. Delete your home Wi-Fi network and begin the connection process again if necessary.
7. Turn off the Mobile data on your smartphone before connecting the appliance.
8. Ensure the wireless network name (SSID) is set correctly and should be a combination of English letters and numbers (Do not use special characters).
9. Ensure the router frequency is set to 2.4 GHz, as only a 2.4 GHz router frequency is supported.
10. Ensure the appliance and the router are not too far apart; if the appliance is too far from the router, the signal may be weak and the connection may fail.

scenario: Dryer fails to dry clothes properly due to a clogged lint filter.
solution_steps:
1. Remove the lint from the filter before every load. With the lint removed, hold the filter up to a light to see if it is dirty or clogged.

2. If the lint filter is full of lint or clogged with fabric softener sheet residue, it can reduce the airflow to the point that the time required to dry clothing will be greatly increased.

3. Always clean the lint filter before and after use.

4. Grip the external filter cover and pull it toward you to remove it.

5. After cleaning the filters, insert it back into place. The appliance will not operate without the lint filter in place.

6. Cleaning the filters will reduce drying time and energy consumption and prevent unnecessary malfunctions.

scenario: Specific dry cycles do not produce the expected drying results due to incorrect cycle selection.
solution_steps:
1. Use the automatic programmes to dry most loads. Electronic sensors measure the temperature of the exhaust to increase or decrease drying temperatures for faster reaction time and tighter temperature control.

2. For best results, use a dedicated cycle suitable for the load. For example, use the Towels cycle for towels and the Jeans cycle for jeans. If you select a dedicated cycle and set the dry option, you will get better results.

3. If you want to dry it more, choose the time-drying of the Dry Only cycle. 

4. For most drying, make sure all clothes are similar in material and thickness.

5. Do not overload the appliance by stuffing too many articles into the drum. Items must be able to tumble freely.

6. Drying times may be longer than those on a vented dryer. For effective drying performance, don't load the drum more than half full.

scenario: Clothes dryer operates inefficiently due to restricted airflow from a lint-clogged filter.
solution_steps:
1. Remove the lint from the filter before every load. With the lint removed, hold the filter up to a light to see if it is dirty or clogged. With some loads that produce high amounts of lint, such as new bath towels, it may be necessary to pause the cycle and clean the filter during the cycle.

3. After cleaning the filters, insert it back into place. The appliance will not operate without the lint filter in place.

scenario: Frozen water inlet or drain hoses in winter prevent the appliance from operating.
solution_steps:
1. Turn off the washer, and unplug the power cord.
2. Turn off the faucets connected to the water inlet hoses.
3. Pour hot water on the frozen faucets to thaw the water inlet hoses and remove the water inlet hoses.
4. Immerse the water inlet hoses in hot water to thaw them.
5. Reconnect the water inlet hoses to the water inlets of the washer and to the faucets.
6. Turn on the faucets.
7. Press the Power button to turn on the washer.
8. Turn the knob to select Spin Only cycle for draining and spinning.
9. Press the Start/Pause button.
10. Pour hot water in the washer drum and close the door.
11. Wait for 1 - 2 hours.
12. Press the Power button.
13. Turn the knob to select Spin Only cycle for draining and spinning.
14. Press the Start/Pause button to make sure the water drains.

scenario: Risk of electric shock due to improper connection of the equipment-grounding conductor.
solution_steps:
1. Check with a qualified electrician or service personnel if you are in doubt whether the appliance is properly grounded.

2. Do not modify the plug provided with the appliance; if it will not fit the outlet, have a proper outlet installed by a qualified electrician.

3. The appliance must be grounded. In the event of a malfunction or breakdown, grounding will reduce the risk of electric shock by providing a path of least resistance for electric current.

4. The appliance is equipped with a cord having an equipment-grounding conductor and a grounding plug. The plug must be plugged into an appropriate outlet that is installed and grounded in accordance with all local codes and ordinances.

5. Improper connection of the equipment grounding conductor can result in risk of electric shock. Check with a qualified electrician or service technician if you are in doubt as to whether the appliance is properly grounded.

6. If the plug does not fit the outlet, have a proper outlet installed by a qualified electrician.

scenario: The appliance may not operate due to external factors like app unavailability or local app store policy changes.
solution_steps:
1. If you experience a problem with your Wi-Fi equipped appliance, it can transmit troubleshooting data to a smartphone using the LG ThinQ application. Launch the LG ThinQ application and select the Smart DiagnosisTM feature in the menu. Follow the instructions provided in the LG ThinQ application.
2. If the Wi-Fi may not connect or the connection may be interrupted because of the home network environment, unplug the appliance and wait about a minute before trying again.
3. If the firewall on your wireless router is enabled, disable the firewall or add an exception to it.
4. The wireless network name (SSID) should be a combination of English letters and numbers. (Do not use special characters.)
5. If the security protocol of the router is set to WEP, network setup may fail. Change the security protocol (WPA2 is recommended), and connect the product again.

6. If all settings and connections are correct, try restarting the appliance and the smartphone to see if this resolves the issue with receiving push alerts.

scenario: The appliance does not level properly on a firm floor, affecting operation.
solution_steps:
1. Position the washer in its final location. Take special care not to pinch, strain, or crush the water and drain hoses. If you have a carpenter’s level, you can use it to check that the washer is level. The slope beneath the washer should not exceed 1 inch, and all 4 leveling feet must rest firmly on the floor.

2. Adjust the leveling feet. Turn all 4 leveling feet in one direction to raise the washer or the other direction to lower it.

3. Check the level again. Push or rock the top edges of the washer gently to make sure the washer does not rock. If the washer rocks, readjust the leveling feet.

4. Tighten the locknuts. Turn the locknuts counterclockwise.

scenario: The Smart Diagnosis feature does not operate due to Wi-Fi unavailability or disconnection.
solution_steps:
1. For reasons not attributable to LGE’s negligence, the service may not operate due to external factors such as Wi-Fi unavailability or Wi-Fi disconnection.
2. If the appliance cannot be connected due to problems with the wireless signal transmission, unplug the appliance and wait about a minute before trying again.
3. The network connection may not work properly depending on the Internet service provider.
4. The Wi-Fi may not connect or the connection may be interrupted because of the home network environment.
5. If the firewall on your wireless router is enabled, disable the firewall or add an exception to it.
6. The wireless network name (SSID) should be a combination of English letters and numbers. (Do not use special characters.)
7. If the security protocol of the router is set to WEP, network setup may fail. Change the security protocol (WPA2 is recommended), and connect the product again.

scenario: Appliance fails to operate due to improper grounding or electrical connection.
solution_steps:
1. Check with a qualified electrician or service personnel if you are in doubt whether the appliance is properly grounded. Do not modify the plug provided with the appliance; if it will not fit the outlet, have a proper outlet installed by a qualified electrician.

2. The appliance must be grounded. In the event of a malfunction or breakdown, grounding will reduce the risk of electric shock by providing a path of least resistance for electric current.

3. Ensure that the plug is plugged into an appropriate outlet that is installed and grounded in accordance with all local codes and ordinances.

4. The appliance must be installed and electrically grounded by qualified service personnel in accordance with local codes.

5. Connect to a properly rated, protected, and sized power circuit to avoid electrical overload.

6. Disconnect the power cord, house fuse, or circuit breaker before installing or servicing the appliance.

7. The power cord of this appliance is equipped with a 3-prong (grounding) plug which mates with a standard 3-prong (grounding) wall outlet to minimize the possibility of electric shock from this appliance.

8. Properly ground the washer to conform with all governing codes and ordinances. Failure to follow this warning can cause serious injury, fire, electric shock, or death.

9. Do not remove the ground prong from the power cord. Do not use an adapter or extension cord. Plug into a grounded 3-prong outlet. Failure to follow this warning can cause serious injury, fire, electric shock, or death.

scenario: Water leakage from the appliance due to clogged water inlet filters.
solution_steps:
1. Unscrew the hot and cold water hoses from the back of the washer.
2. Remove the filters from the water valves carefully.
   - Use pliers to pull out the filters from the water valves.
3. Remove foreign objects and soak the filters in white vinegar or a lime scale remover.
   - If using a lime scale remover, follow the manufacturer’s instructions. Be careful not to damage the filters while cleaning them.
4. Rinse filters thoroughly and press them back into place.
5. Flush then reattach the water hoses.
   - Before reattaching the water inlet hoses, flush them by running several gallons of water through them into a bucket or drain, preferably with the faucets wide open for maximum flow.

   - To set the minutes, press the CLOCK button again. The minutes in the LED control panel will start flashing.
   - Press and hold the SET button to scroll through the numbers. Release the button once the desired minutes is displayed.
   - The time currently set will be saved if no button is pressed for 10 seconds.

   - Press the AUTO ON button (b) for a minimum of 3 seconds. The hours in the LED panel will start flashing.
   - Press and hold the SET button (e) to scroll through the numbers. Release the button once the desired hour is displayed.
   - To set the minutes, press the AUTO ON button. The minutes in the LED control panel will start flashing.
   - Press and hold the SET button to scroll through the numbers. Release the button once the desired minutes is displayed.
   - Press the AUTO ON button again to save the desired time.
   - If during the setting process no button is pressed for 10 seconds, the auto on time currently set will be saved.

scenario: Using an incorrect filter type leads to coffee overflow.
solution_steps:
1. Use only the Cuisinart® Gold-Tone Commercial-Style Filter or standard cone-shaped paper filter with this unit.
2. Ensure that a paper filter is completely open and fully inserted in the basket. It may help to fold and flatten the seams of a paper filter beforehand.
3. Replace the filter basket in the filter basket holder, and press firmly on the cover to be sure it closes securely.
4. Do not use other gold-tone permanent filters, as they may cause the coffeemaker to overflow.
5. Ensure the maximum capacity for ground coffee does not exceed 12 tablespoons for this coffeemaker to prevent overflow.

scenario: The unit fails to operate in a 120-volt outlet.
solution_steps:

2. Verify that the plug is fully inserted into the outlet. If the plug does not fit fully, reverse the plug and try again. As indicated in the manual: "This appliance has a polarized plug (one blade is wider than the other). To reduce the risk of electric shock, this plug will fit in a polarized outlet only one way. If the plug does not fit fully in the outlet, reverse the plug."

3. If the plug still does not fit, do not modify the plug. Instead, "contact a qualified electrician."

4. Check the cord and plug for any visible damage. As per the manual: "Do not operate any appliance with a damaged cord or plug or after the appliance malfunctions or has been dropped or damaged in any manner."

5. If the appliance is still not operating, "return appliance to the nearest Cuisinart Repair Center for examination, repair, or electrical or mechanical adjustment."

6. Ensure that the unit is not being used with unauthorized accessories, as the manual states, "This warranty expressly excludes any defects or damages caused by attempted use of this unit with a converter, as well as use with accessories, replacement parts or repair service other than those authorized by Cuisinart."

scenario: The coffee continues streaming from the filter for an excessive time after the brew cycle.
solution_steps:
1. After brewing, press the power button to turn off. When the brewing cycle has been completed, 5 beeps will sound. Coffee will continue to stream from the filter for several seconds.
2. Use caution. The bottom of the thermal carafe is hot to touch for several seconds after brewing.
3. Note: Reservoir cover may be hot during and directly after brewing. Wait at least 10 minutes before opening.
4. Clogging and backing up of water and/or coffee in the filter basket can occur under any or a combination of any of the following conditions: using too finely ground coffee, using two or more paper filters, using the gold-tone filter in conjunction with a paper filter, not properly cleaning coffee grounds from the gold-tone filter, or allowing coffee grounds to spill over the filter.
5. Caution: Never open the reservoir cover during the brewing cycle, even if no water is draining from the filter basket, since extremely hot water/coffee can spill out from the basket and cause injury. If water/coffee is not draining from the filter basket during the brewing cycle, unplug the unit and wait 10 minutes before opening the reservoir cover and checking the basket.

scenario: Following a power failure, the clock must be reset for the coffee maker to function properly.
solution_steps:
1. When you initially plug in the coffee maker, the unit will beep and “12:00” will flash on the LCD display for a few seconds. Press immediately the h/min button (o) to set the current hour. If “12:00” starts to flash, press the PROG button (n) for a few seconds until the “12:00” flashes again. Then press the h/min button (o) to set the current hour. There are AM and PM indicators on the top right side of the LCD screen. To set the current minutes, press the PROG button (n) and then press the h/min button (o) until the correct minutes appear on the LCD display. After 5 seconds, the unit will beep and the time will stop flashing.

2. At any other time, you can set the clock or change the set time by pressing and holding the h/min button (o). The unit will beep and “12:00” will flash on the LCD display. Use the h/min button (o) to set the current hour. There are AM and PM indicators on the top right side of the LCD screen. To set the current minutes, press the PROG button (n) and then press the h/min button (o) until the correct minutes appear on the LCD display. After 5 seconds, the unit will beep and the time will stop flashing.

scenario: Brewing takes longer than usual, indicating the need for descaling due to mineral buildup.
solution_steps:
1. "We recommend descaling your unit with a solution of white vinegar and cold water or a suitable descaling agent. A solution of two tablespoons of white vinegar to one carafe of cold water works best."
2. "Pour this solution into the water tank, and follow your normal operating instructions, without a filter in the filter basket."
3. "When the brew cycle is finished, empty the carafe and rinse with water."
4. "Refill the water reservoir with cold water only and repeat the brew cycle with water only, twice more. This will rinse out any remaining vinegar solution."
5. "We strongly recommend decalcifying your coffee maker any time the brewing time slows down or when you begin to notice excessive steaming."
6. "The frequency of decalcifying will depend on the hardness of your water. We suggest decalcifying approximately every 80 brew cycles if you have soft water or every 40 brew cycles if you have hard water."
conversation:

HomeHelper: It sounds like there might be a mineral buildup causing the slowdown. Have you ever descaled your coffee maker?

HomeHelper: Descaling involves cleaning out the mineral deposits using a solution. You can use two tablespoons of white vinegar mixed with a carafe of cold water.

HomeHelper: Yes, pour the solution into the water tank. Then run a brew cycle just like you normally would, but without a filter in the basket.

User: Got it. What do I do once it's done brewing?

HomeHelper: Once the cycle finishes, empty the carafe and rinse it with water. Then, refill the water reservoir with cold water only.

User: How often should I be doing this descaling process?

scenario: The coffee maker requires periodic descaling to maintain optimal performance, especially with hard water.
solution_steps:
1. We recommend descaling your unit with a solution of white vinegar and cold water or a suitable descaling agent.

2. A solution of two tablespoons of white vinegar to one carafe of cold water works best.

3. Pour this solution into the water tank, and follow your normal operating instructions, without a filter in the filter basket.

4. When the brew cycle is finished, empty the carafe and rinse with water.

5. Refill the water reservoir with cold water only and repeat the brew cycle with water only, twice more. This will rinse out any remaining vinegar solution.

scenario: The over ice button does not engage, preventing the brewing of iced coffee.
solution_steps:
1. Ensure that the coffeemaker is plugged in.
2. Fill the tumbler to the "WATER" marking with clean, filtered water.
3. Lift the lid of the unit and pour the water into the reservoir.
4. Place the reusable coffee filter (or standard 5-cup basket-style paper filter) into the brew basket.
5. Using the ICED side of the coffee scoop, pour 1 scoop of grounds into the reusable coffee filter. Close the lid.
6. Fill the tumbler with large ice cubes to the "ICE" marking.
7. Place tumbler full of ice under brew spout and press the “OVER ICE” button – ensure the LED is illuminated.
8. If the button indicator light flashes when pressing “OVER ICE,” wait a few more seconds for the heater to cool off before pressing again.

scenario: The plastic components become discolored or damaged after exposure to hot steam.
solution_steps:
1. Place the appliance on a hard, flat, level surface to avoid interruption of airflow underneath the coffeemaker.

2. Keep the area above the appliance clear during use, as hot steam will escape the appliance.

3. All lids should be closed during use.

4. Scalding may occur if the lid is removed or brew basket door is opened during or immediately after the brewing cycles. Contents may be hot. Allow to cool before opening the lid.

solution_steps:

2. To increase the length of the power cord: grasp the power cord (not the power plug) and gently lift it out of the slot, then pull it away from the coffeemaker.

3. To decrease the length of the power cord: Grasp the power cord (not the power plug), lift it out of the slot and gently feed it into the coffeemaker.

4. Lock the cord in the slot when finished.

scenario: The needle in the pack holder gets clogged, obstructing water flow.
solution_steps:
1. Unscrew the base from the reservoir. Turn the base over and use your finger to push the bottom of the used single serve pack out of the holder. Discard the pack. CAUTION! There is a sharp needle in the pack holder. To prevent injury, do not place fingers in the pack holder.

2. Pull the pump off of the reservoir and wash the pump, reservoir, and base in warm, soapy water. Rinse and dry. Do not wash the MyJo coffee maker in the dishwasher.

3. There is a silicone valve located in the inside bottom of the reservoir. If you notice the valve contains coffee grounds or residue, you should remove it for cleaning. The easiest way to do this is by gently poking the valve at an angle from underneath the reservoir with a blunt object, such as a Q-tip* cotton swab or the eraser end of a pencil. Note: There is a slit in the center of the valve so push gently on the outer edge of the valve.

4. Wash the coffee maker parts in warm, soapy water. Rinse thoroughly to remove any soap residue. Do not wash the MyJo coffee maker in the dishwasher. CAUTION! There is a sharp needle in the pack holder which is designed to puncture the single serve pack. To prevent injury, do not place fingers in the pack holder.

scenario: Coffee grounds overflow during brewing, leading to a mess.
solution_steps:
1. If using your own coffee grounds rather than a single serve pack, ensure you are using the MyJo Cup, as it is the only cup designed to work with the MyJo coffee maker. Do not use any other brand of cup. 

2. Verify that the top and bottom of the pack are pierced. Carefully unscrew the reservoir from the base. For packs with plastic bottoms, push down to ensure the bottom is pierced. Check the top. If you do not see a small hole in the middle, make one with a knife. Reassemble and resume pumping.

3. Ensure you are applying a gentle steady pressure during pumping to prevent any breakage or overflow that might occur due to excessive force. 

4. Make sure your mug is the right size before pumping your coffee. The diameter of the inner rim of the mug should be at least 2¼˝ but not more than 3¾˝ wide. 

5. Position the coffee maker and mug directly in front of you. Grasp the coffee maker base with one hand and place the palm of your other hand on the pump cap. If using a tall travel mug, grasp the top portion of the mug instead of the coffee maker base.

scenario: Articles cleaned with flammable substances like gasoline may ignite or explode when dried.
solution_steps:
1. Read all instructions before using this appliance.

2. Do not dry items that have been previously cleaned, washed, soaked, or spotted with gasoline, dry cleaning solvents, or other flammable or explosive substances. They emit vapors that could ignite or explode. 

3. Any material that has been in contact with a cleaning solvent or flammable liquids or solids should not be placed in the dryer until all traces of these flammable liquids or solids and their fumes have been removed. 

4. Items containing foam rubber (which may be labeled latex foam) or similarly textured rubberlike materials must not be dried on a heat setting. Heated foam rubber materials can, under certain circumstances, ignite spontaneously.

scenario: The appliance is unable to dry articles that have been cleaned with flammable substances, risking fire or explosion.
solution_steps:
1. Do not dry articles that have been previously cleaned, washed, soaked, or spotted with gasoline, dry-cleaning solvents, or other flammable or explosive substances, as they give off vapours that could ignite or explode.
2. Any material that has been in contact with a cleaning solvent or flammable liquids or solids should not be placed in the dryer until all traces of these flammable liquids or solids and their fumes have been removed. There are many highly flammable items used in homes, such as acetone, denatured alcohol, gasoline, kerosene, some liquid household cleaners, some spot removers, turpentine, waxes, and wax removers.
3. Items containing foam rubber (which may be labeled latex foam) or similarly textured rubberlike materials must not be dried on a heat setting. Heated foam rubber materials can, under certain circumstances, ignite spontaneously.
4. Do not place items exposed to cooking oils in your dryer. Items contaminated with cooking oils may contribute to a chemical reaction that could cause a load to catch fire. To reduce the risk of fire due to contaminated loads, the final part of a tumble dryer cycle occurs without heat (cool down period). Avoid stopping a tumble dryer before the end of the drying cycle unless all items are quickly removed and spread out so that the heat is dissipated.

However, drying time may be extended or the drying performance may be degraded.

6. Do not use a poor exhaust system because it slows down the dryer’s performance.

7. Do not use excessively long ducts that have multiple elbows.

8. Do not use crushed or clogged venting or ducts.

scenario: Risk of fire or explosion when drying articles cleaned with flammable substances.
solution_steps:
1. Do not dry articles that have been previously cleaned in, washed in, soaked in, or spotted with gasoline, dry-cleaning solvents, or other flammable or explosive substances, as they give off vapours that could ignite or explode.

2. Any material that has been in contact with a cleaning solvent or flammable liquids or solids should not be placed in the dryer until all traces of these flammable liquids or solids and their fumes have been removed.

3. To reduce the risk of fire due to contaminated loads, the final part of a tumble dryer cycle occurs without heat (cool down period). Avoid stopping a tumble dryer before the end of the drying cycle unless all items are quickly removed and spread out so that the heat is dissipated.

4. Do not place items exposed to cooking oils in your dryer. Items contaminated with cooking oils may contribute to a chemical reaction that could cause a load to catch fire.

1. Do not dry articles that have been previously cleaned in, washed in, soaked in, or spotted with gasoline, dry-cleaning solvents, or other flammable or explosive substances, as they give off vapours that could ignite or explode.

2. Any material that has been in contact with a cleaning solvent or flammable liquids or solids should not be placed in the dryer until all traces of these flammable liquids or solids and their fumes have been removed.

3. To reduce the risk of fire due to contaminated loads, the final part of a tumble dryer cycle occurs without heat (cool down period). Avoid stopping a tumble dryer before the end of the drying cycle unless all items are quickly removed and spread out so that the heat is dissipated.

4. Do not place items exposed to cooking oils in your dryer. Items contaminated with cooking oils may contribute to a chemical reaction that could cause a load to catch fire.
conversation:
User: Hi HomeHelper, I just read that drying clothes with flammable substances can be dangerous. Can you help me understand why?

HomeHelper: Absolutely! When clothes are cleaned with substances like gasoline or dry-cleaning solvents, they can release vapors that might ignite or even explode in the dryer.

User: Wow, I didn't realize that. So, what should I do if my clothes have been in contact with those substances?

HomeHelper: First, make sure that all traces of those flammable liquids and their fumes are completely removed before placing the clothes in the dryer. It's crucial for safety.

User: Got it. Is there a specific way to ensure all traces are gone?

HomeHelper: You can wash the items thoroughly with a strong detergent and let them air out completely. Make sure they don't smell like the solvent before drying them.

HomeHelper: Yes, avoid stopping the dryer before the cycle ends unless you can quickly spread out the clothes to dissipate the heat. The cool down period at the end helps reduce fire risk.

HomeHelper: It's best not to place items with cooking oil in the dryer. The oils can cause a chemical reaction that might lead to a fire.

scenario: Foam rubber or rubber-like materials do not dry properly and should not be heated.
solution_steps:
1. Do not dry items containing foam rubber or similarly textured rubberlike materials on a heat setting, as "heated foam rubber materials can, under certain circumstances, ignite spontaneously."

2. Instead of using heat, refer to the care label instructions for alternative drying methods, such as air drying or using a low temperature setting if applicable. 

3. Always ensure that "foam rubber (rug backs, stuffed toys, shoulder pads, etc.)" are not subjected to a heated drying cycle to avoid damage or risk of fire.

4. If drying plastics, such as shower curtains or outdoor furniture covers, use "TIME DRY and the Low temperature settings depending on the care label instructions."

5. Remember that drying a rubber item with heat may damage it or cause a fire.

scenario: Door removal required before discarding the appliance.
solution_steps:

2. Unplug the power cord.
3. Remove two door hinge screws.
4. Lift the door and remove it.
5. Remove the two screws that are above and below the cut-out in the frame front.

scenario: Risk of fire if drying articles previously cleaned with flammable substances.
solution_steps:
1. Do not dry articles that have been previously cleaned in, washed in, soaked in, or spotted with gasoline, dry-cleaning solvents, or other flammable or explosive substances, as they give off vapours that could ignite or explode.

2. Any material that has been in contact with a cleaning solvent or flammable liquids or solids should not be placed in the dryer until all traces of these flammable liquids or solids and their fumes have been removed.

3. Items containing foam rubber (which may be labeled latex foam) or similarly textured rubberlike materials must not be dried on a heat setting. Heated foam rubber materials can, under certain circumstances, ignite spontaneously.

scenario: Articles cleaned or soaked in flammable substances ignite or explode when dried.
solution_steps:
1. "Do not dry articles that have been previously cleaned in, washed in, soaked in, or spotted with gasoline, dry-cleaning solvents, or other flammable or explosive substances, as they give off vapours that could ignite or explode."

2. "Any material that has been in contact with a cleaning solvent or flammable liquids or solids should not be placed in the dryer until all traces of these flammable liquids or solids and their fumes have been removed."

3. "There are many highly flammable items used in homes, such as acetone, denatured alcohol, gasoline, kerosene, some liquid household cleaners, some spot removers, turpentine, waxes, and wax removers."

4. "Items containing foam rubber (which may be labeled latex foam) or similarly textured rubberlike materials must not be dried on a heat setting."

5. "Residual oil on clothing can ignite spontaneously. The potential for spontaneous combustion increases when items containing vegetable oil or cooking oil are exposed to heat."

6. "Washing these items in hot water with extra detergent will reduce, but not eliminate, the hazard."

7. "Always use the Cool Down cycle for these items to reduce their temperature."

8. "Never remove these items from the dryer hot or interrupt the drying cycle until the items have run through the Cool Down cycle."

9. "Never pile or stack these items when they are hot."

10. "Avoid stopping a tumble dryer before the end of the drying cycle unless all items are quickly removed and spread out so that the heat is dissipated."

scenario: Heat drying articles containing foam rubber or similar materials results in damage or hazards.

scenario: Smart Diagnosis feature does not work because the appliance is not properly connected to Wi-Fi.
solution_steps:
1. Find the Wi-Fi network connected to your smartphone and remove it, then register your appliance on LG ThinQ.
2. Turn off the Mobile data of your smartphone and register the appliance using the Wi-Fi network.
3. Ensure that the wireless network name (SSID) is a combination of English letters and numbers, and does not use special characters.
4. Set the wireless router to 2.4 GHz as only a 2.4 GHz router frequency is supported. To check the router frequency, check with your Internet service provider or the router manufacturer.
5. If the appliance is having trouble connecting to the Wi-Fi network, it may be too far from the router. Purchase a Wi-Fi repeater (range extender) to improve the Wi-Fi signal strength.
6. To verify the Wi-Fi connection, check that f icon on the control panel is lit.

scenario: Clothes take too long to dry, even with appropriate control settings.
solution_steps:
1. Remove the lint from the lint filter after every cycle. With the lint removed, hold the lint filter up to a light to see if it is dirty or clogged. With some loads that produce high amounts of lint, such as new bath towels, it may be necessary to pause the cycle and clean the filter during the cycle.

2. Reset circuit breaker or replace fuse. Do not increase fuse capacity. If the problem is a circuit overload, have it corrected by a qualified electrician.

3. Divide extra large loads into smaller loads for better drying performance and efficiency.

4. Separate heavy items from lightweight items. Larger and heavier items take longer to dry. Light items in a load with heavy items can fool the appliance.

3. Remove the inner filter.
4. Open the outer filter by unfolding in the direction of the arrow grasping the top edge of the outer filter.
5. Clean the residual lint using vacuum cleaner or washing under running water. Dry the filter completely if the filter is moist.
6. Close the outer filter while pushing the side a of the filter. Ensure the side of the filter is closed properly.
7. Reinsert the both lint filters.
8. Pull out the inner filter from the outer filter and then open the inner filter by unfolding it in the direction of the arrow.
9. Clean a large cluster of lint first, then clean the residual lint using vacuum cleaner or washing under running water. Dry the filter completely if the filter is moist.
10. After drying the inner filter completely, close the filter by pushing down its center. Ensure the left and right side of the inner filter is closed properly.
11. Insert the inner filter into the outer filter.
12. After cleaning the lint filter, insert them in a place. If the lint filter is not in the appliance, you cannot operate the appliance.

scenario: Clothes take too long to dry even when using the correct cycle settings.
solution_steps:
1. Use the appropriate control settings for the type of load you are drying. Some loads may require an adjustment of the dry level setting for proper drying.
2. Remove the lint from the lint filter after every cycle. With the lint removed, hold the lint filter up to a light to see if it is dirty or clogged. With some loads that produce high amounts of lint, such as new bath towels, it may be necessary to pause the cycle and clean the filter during the cycle.
3. Reset circuit breaker or replace fuse. Do not increase fuse capacity. If the problem is a circuit overload, have it corrected by a qualified electrician.
4. Divide extra large loads into smaller loads for better drying performance and efficiency.
5. Separate heavy items from lightweight items. Larger and heavier items take longer to dry. Light items in a load with heavy items can fool the appliance.

scenario: Lint filter becomes clogged, affecting drying performance.
solution_steps:
1. Remove the lint from the lint filter after every cycle. With the lint removed, hold the lint filter up to a light to see if it is dirty or clogged.

2. If the lint filter is still dirty or clogged, follow these steps to clean it:
   
3. Pull out the outer filter.

4. Remove the inner filter.

5. Open the outer filter by unfolding in the direction of the arrow grasping the top edge of the outer filter.

6. Clean the residual lint using a vacuum cleaner or washing under running water.

7. Dry the filter completely if the filter is moist. Failure to do so, odour may occur in the appliance.

8. Close the outer filter while pushing the side of the filter. Ensure the side of the filter is closed properly.

9. Pull out the inner filter from the outer filter and then open the inner filter by unfolding it in the direction of the arrow.

10. Clean a large cluster of lint first, then clean the residual lint using a vacuum cleaner or washing under running water.

11. Dry the filter completely if the filter is moist. Failure to do so, odour may occur in the appliance.

12. After drying the inner filter completely, close the filter by pushing down its center. Ensure the left and right side of the inner filter is closed properly.

13. Insert the inner filter into the outer filter.

14. Reinsert both lint filters into their place. Do not load or remove any clothes when the lint filter is not in place.

scenario: The Smart Diagnosis feature does not work due to external factors like Wi-Fi disconnection.
solution_steps:
1. Ensure that your home appliance and smartphone are connected to the Wi-Fi network. If they are not, check the following:

   a. If the password for the Wi-Fi that you are trying to connect to is incorrect, find the Wi-Fi network connected to your smartphone and remove it, then register your appliance on LG ThinQ.

   b. If mobile data for your smartphone is turned on, turn off the Mobile data of your smartphone and register the appliance using the Wi-Fi network.

   c. Check if the wireless network name (SSID) is set incorrectly. The wireless network name (SSID) should be a combination of English letters and numbers. Do not use special characters.

   d. Verify if the router frequency is not 2.4 GHz. Only a 2.4 GHz router frequency is supported. Set the wireless router to 2.4 GHz and connect the appliance to the wireless router. To check the router frequency, check with your Internet service provider or the router manufacturer.

   e. If the distance between the appliance and the router is too far, try moving them closer together.

scenario: Appliance fails to start because the lint filter is not inserted properly.
solution_steps:
1. Unload all of the laundries from the appliance before pulling out the lint filter.

2. Pull out the inner filter from the outer filter.

3. Clean the lint filter by removing lint after every cycle.

4. Hold the lint filter up to a light to see if it is dirty or clogged. Clean the filter if necessary.

5. If the lint has accumulated, a chime will sound and the Filter Cleaning indicator will blink. Clean the inner filter by first cleaning a large cluster of lint, then clean the residual lint using a vacuum cleaner or washing under running water.

6. Dry the filter completely if the filter is moist to prevent odor in the appliance.

7. After drying the inner filter completely, close the filter by pushing down its center. Ensure the left and right side of the inner filter is closed properly.

8. Insert the inner filter into the outer filter.

9. After cleaning the lint filter, insert it in place. If the lint filter is not in the appliance, you cannot operate the appliance.

scenario: The waste water pump is blocked by large food remnants or foreign objects.
solution_steps:

6. Check impeller wheel and remove any foreign objects.
7. Place cover in the original position and press down until it engages (click).
8. Install filters.
9. Re-insert baskets.

scenario: The rinse aid refill indicator doesn't function, leading to improper drying results.

scenario: The rinse aid refill indicator doesn't function, leading to improper drying results.
solution_steps:
1. Check if the use of combined detergents with a rinse-aid component impairs the low rinse-aid indicator 8 on the control panel or the text on the front display. If so, the displays can be switched off. 
2. Proceed as described under “Setting amount of rinse aid” and select setting 0. The instructions for setting the amount of rinse aid are as follows:
   a. Switch on ON/OFF switch.
   b. Press and hold the Info button for 3 seconds until the following text appears on the front display: "Scroll with < > Set with - + Leave with Setup 3 sec."
   c. Press the > button repeatedly until "Rinse aid dispenser" appears on the front display.
   d. Adjust the setting using the setting buttons + and -.
   e. Press and hold the Info button for 3 seconds. The chosen setting has now been stored.
3. If the rinse aid refill indicator is still not functioning, ensure there is no rinse aid. If there is no rinse aid, refill rinse aid.
4. If these steps do not resolve the issue, refer to the chapter “Rinse aid” on Page 22 for further instructions.

scenario: The salt refill indicator displays inaccurately, affecting the softening of water.
solution_steps:
1. Check if the refill indicator for salt is lit: If the indicator is lit, it means there is no salt. Refill with special salt as stated in the manual: "As soon as the low salt indicator @ is lit on the control panel or is requested on the front display * )B, salt should be topped up."

2. If the indicator is not lit but you suspect it is inaccurate, verify if the refill indicator is switched off: "Refill indicator switched off. Activation/deactivation (see chapter “Water softening system/Special salt” ~ Page 20 or “Rinse aid” ~ Page 22 )."

3. Ensure you're using the correct type of salt: "Sensor does not detect salt tablets. Use different special salt."

4. Top up the salt correctly:
   - Undo the screw plug on the dispenser.
   - Fill the dispenser with water (required only when switching on the appliance for the first time).
   - Add salt as illustrated (do not use table salt or tablets). "The water is displaced and runs out."

5. Always refill with special salt immediately before switching on the appliance to ensure proper function: "This ensures that overrun special salt solution is immediately washed out and does not corrode the rinsing tank."

6. Verify that detergent has not been mistakenly added to the salt dispenser: "Detergent will destroy the water softening system! Never pour detergent into the salt dispenser."

scenario: Wi-Fi connection issues prevent the appliance from connecting to the Home Connect server.
solution_steps:
1. If the connection to the router fails, the WLAN H display flashes on the display.
2. If your dishwasher does not connect to the home network, you can also operate the dishwasher manually by pressing the buttons.
3. To be able to operate the appliance via Home Connect, the Home Connect App must be installed on your mobile terminal device. Observe the supplied Home Connect documents.
4. You can set your dishwasher by pressing the remote start button }h or proceed as follows:
   a. Switch on ON/OFF switch (.
   b. Press and hold the Info button { ` for 3 seconds until the following text appears on the front display )B: Scroll with < > Set with - + Leave with Setup 3 sec.
   c. Press the > )2 button repeatedly until the required setting appears on the front display )B.
   d. Adjust the setting using the buttons + and - P.
   e. Press Info button { ` for 3 seconds. The chosen setting has now been stored in your dishwasher.
5. In the Wi-Fi menu you can activate the wireless network connection with “on” and deactivate it with “off”.
6. The “Network login” menu option is not available unless you have activated Wi-Fi.
7. In the “Network login” menu, you can select between “Autom./WPS” and “Manual” to connect the dishwasher to your home network.
   a. Automatic: Connect to the home network using the WPS function of your router.
   b. Manual: Connect your mobile terminal device to the Home Connect network. The network settings are then manually entered using the Home Connect App to connect to your home network.
8. If you did not deactivate the connection to the Home Connect server, check your Internet connection.
9. If the Home Connect Assistant was aborted during start-up, press the remote start button }h again.

scenario: The door opener mechanism malfunctions and does not open the door.
solution_steps:

2. If the door is difficult to open, ensure that the child-proof lock is deactivated.
3. If the door cannot be closed or opened due to installation, check the appliance installation: Door or attached parts must close without obstruction.
4. If the door lock has been activated, try to close the door with increased force.
5. If the issue persists and the door function is impaired, stop operating the appliance, pull out the mains plug or switch off the fuse, turn off the tap, and call customer service.

scenario: Large food remnants or foreign objects block the waste water pump.
solution_steps:
1. Disconnect the dishwasher from the power supply.
2. Take out top basket 12 and bottom basket 1j.
3. Remove the filters 1Z.
4. Scoop out water, use a sponge if required.
5. Prise off the pump cover (as shown) using a spoon. Grip the pump cover by the crosspiece and lift diagonally inwards (1). Remove cover completely.
6. Check impeller wheel and remove any foreign objects.
7. Place pump cover in the original position (2) and press down until it engages (3).
8. Install filters.
9. Re-insert baskets.

scenario: The detergent dispenser lock does not engage, preventing proper detergent release.

The manual states: "Cover on the detergent dispenser cannot be closed. – Detergent dispenser overfilled or mechanism blocked by sticky detergent residue."

2. Ensure the detergent dispenser is dry when filling. The manual mentions: "Detergent residue in the detergent dispenser. – Dispenser was damp when filled."

3. If the detergent dispenser is still closed, press the lock to open the detergent dispenser as per the manual: "If the detergent dispenser 9' is still closed, press the lock 9* to open the detergent dispenser."

4. Pour detergent into the dry detergent dispenser 9" only (insert tablet flat, not on its edge). The manual provides dosage instructions: "Dosage: see manufacturer’s instructions on the packaging. The graduated detergent dispenser 9' helps you add the correct amount of powder or liquid detergent. Usually 20 ml–25 ml are adequate for normal soiling. If using tablets, one tablet is adequate."

5. Close the cover on the detergent dispenser by sliding it up until the lock engages without difficulty. The manual instructs: "Close the cover on the detergent dispenser by sliding it up until the lock engages without difficulty."

6. If the issue persists, contact the detergent manufacturers’ helpline for further questions, as suggested in the manual: "If you have further questions, we recommend that you contact the detergent manufacturers’ helpline."

scenario: Tableware is not dry due to no rinse aid being used or the dosage being set too low.
solution_steps:
1. Add "Rinse aid" as directed on Page 27: "If the rinse aid refill indicator lights up, top up with rinse aid. Only use rinse aid for domestic dishwashers."
2. To add rinse aid, follow these steps: 
   a. "Press the catch on the lid of the dispenser for rinse aid and lift."
   b. "Add rinse aid up to the max mark."
   c. "If rinse aid spills out, remove it from the tub. Spilled rinse aid can cause excessive frothing during the wash cycle."
   d. "Close the lid of the dispenser for rinse aid. The lid clicks into position."
3. Set the amount of rinse aid to be dispensed as described: 
   a. "Press ⁠."
   b. "To open the basic settings, press for 3 seconds. The display shows Hxx."
   c. "Press repeatedly until the display shows the value set at the factory r04."
   d. "Press repeatedly until the right amount of rinse aid has been set."

scenario: The oven fails to start cooking if the door is not completely closed.

5. If Stop/Reset has been touched accidentally, program the oven again.

scenario: The oven stops cooking unexpectedly, possibly due to an incorrect program or accidental pressing of Stop/Reset.
solution_steps:
1. Confirm that the oven door is closed completely.
2. If the door is closed, verify if Start/Set was touched after programming. If not, touch Start/Set to begin cooking.
3. Check if another program is already entered into the oven. If so, touch Stop/Reset to cancel the previous program and enter a new program.
4. Ensure that the program is correct; if not, program again according to the Owner’s manual.
5. Determine if Stop/Reset was touched accidentally. If it was, program the oven again.

scenario: The oven causes interference with radio, TV, or other wireless equipment during operation.
solution_steps:
1. Increase the spacing distance between the microwave oven and other product receiving the interference.
2. If possible, use a properly installed receiver antenna and/or reorient the receiving antenna of the other product receiving the interference.
3. Plug the microwave oven into a different outlet from the other product receiving the interference.
4. Clean door and sealing surfaces of the oven. (See Care and Cleaning of Your Microwave Oven)

scenario: Steam accumulates on the oven door and warm air comes from the vents, which is normal and should be wiped dry after use.
solution_steps:
1. During cooking, steam and warm air are given off from the food. Most of the steam and warm air are removed from the oven by the air which circulates in the oven cavity. However, some steam will condense on cooler surfaces such as the oven door. This is normal.

2. After use, the oven should be wiped dry.

3. Wipe the oven door with a soft dry cloth when steam accumulates inside or around the outside of the oven door.

4. Always clean the flat table after cooling down with a mild detergent and wipe to dry.

5. If the Control Panel becomes wet, clean it with a soft dry cloth. Do not use harsh detergents or abrasives.

scenario: The microwave does not operate when using wooden or ceramic containers with metallic inlays.
solution_steps:
1. Never use metal or metal trimmed utensils in your microwave oven.

2. Microwaves cannot penetrate metal. They will bounce off any metal object in the oven and cause arcing, an alarming phenomenon that resembles lightning.

3. Check the utensils are suitable for use in microwave ovens before use.

4. If you have any doubts about a particular utensil, there’s a simple way to find out if it can be used in your microwave oven. Place the utensil in question next to a glass bowl filled with water in the microwave oven. Microwave at power HIGH for 1 minute.

5. If the water heats up but the utensil remains cool to the touch, the utensil is microwave-safe. However, if the water does not change temperature but the utensil becomes warm, microwaves are being absorbed by the utensil and it is not safe for use in the microwave oven.

1. "Small amounts of food require shorter cooking or heating time. If normal times are allowed they may overheat and burn."

4. "Press MICRO twice to select 80%(720W) power."

5. "Adjust the cooking time according to the power level and the amount of food being cooked."

HomeHelper: Yes, your microwave has 5 power levels to help you control the cooking process better. This can be really useful for smaller amounts of food.

User: Oh, I didn't know about the power levels. How do I change them?

HomeHelper: You can press the MICRO button twice to select the 80% power level, which is 720 watts. This should give you more flexibility.

User: Got it. So, after I select the power level, what should I do next?

HomeHelper: Once you've set the power level, adjust the cooking time accordingly. The power level and amount of food both influence how long you should cook it.

User: That sounds straightforward. I'll give it a try next time. Thanks for the help!

HomeHelper: You're welcome! If you have any more questions or need further assistance, feel free to reach out. Happy cooking!

scenario: Using ceramic containers with metallic inlays can cause arcing and potentially damage the appliance.
solution_steps:
1. "Never use metal or metal trimmed utensils in your microwave oven."
2. "Microwaves cannot penetrate metal. They will bounce off any metal object in the oven and cause arcing, an alarming phenomenon that resembles lightning."
3. "Utensils should be checked to ensure that they are suitable for use in microwave ovens."
4. "There’s a simple way to find out if it can be used in your microwave oven. Place the utensil in question next to a glass bowl filled with water in the microwave oven. Microwave at power HIGH for 1 minute. If the water heats up but the utensil remains cool to the touch, the utensil is microwave-safe. However, if the water does not change temperature but the utensil becomes warm, microwaves are being absorbed by the utensil and it is not safe for use in the microwave oven."

scenario: Grease accumulation on the vent-hood filter.
solution_steps:
1. To remove the filter, push the front of the grease filter case where it says 'PUSH'.
2. Pull the filter case out of the microwave oven.
3. Remove the filter from the filter case by widening the case, as shown below. Then, soak the grease filter in hot water mixed with a mild detergent. Rinse well and shake to dry. If necessary, brush the filter lightly to remove embedded dirt. When the filter is dry, put it back in the filter case.
4. To re-insert the filter into the microwave oven, slide the filter case into the frame slot, and then push it inside.
5. Clean ventilating hoods frequently - Grease should not be allowed to accumulate on the hood of the filter.

scenario: Risk of electric shock due to improper grounding plug use.
solution_steps:
1. Plug into a grounded, 3 pronged outlet. Do not remove the third (grounding) prong. Do not use an adaptor or otherwise thwart the safety function of the grounding plug.
2. Consult a qualified electrician or service person if you do not understand the grounding instructions or if you are not sure if the appliance is properly grounded.
3. Do not ground the appliance to a gas pipe, plastic water pipe, or telephone line. This may result in electric shock, fire, an explosion, or problems with the product.
4. Never plug the power cord into a socket that is not grounded correctly and make sure that it is grounded in accordance with local and national codes.
5. Do not cut or remove the third (ground) prong from the power cord under any circumstances.
6. The microwave requires a separate branch circuit single grounded outlet of at least 15 A and max of 20 A.
7. Plug the power cord into a properly grounded 3 pronged outlet. Your oven should be the only appliance connected to this circuit. Sharing a wall socket with other appliances, using a power strip, or extending the power cord may result in electric shock or fire.
8. Do not use an electric transformer. It may result in electric shock or fire.
9. Ensure that the voltage, frequency, and current provided match the product's specifications. Failing to do so may result in electric shock or fire.

scenario: Corrosive cleaning agents may damage the vent-hood filter.
solution_steps:
1. Use care when cleaning the vent-hood filter. Corrosive cleaning agents, such as lye-based oven cleaner, may damage the filter.
2. The grease filters should be removed and cleaned at least once every four months or as required.
3. To remove the filter, slide it to the left (or right) using the tab.
4. Soak the grease filter in hot water and a mild detergent. Rinse well and shake to dry. Brushing the filter lightly can remove embedded dirt.
5. Do not use ammonia or put the grease filter in the microwave oven. The aluminum will darken.
6. To re-install the filter, slide it into the frame slot on the left (or right), and then push it upwards and to the right (or left) to lock it.

HomeHelper: Now, soak the filter in hot water with a mild detergent. This will help clean it without causing damage.

HomeHelper: Yes, brushing it lightly can help remove any embedded dirt. Just be gentle with it.  
User: Okay, I’ve done that. How do I dry it?  
HomeHelper: After rinsing it well, shake it to remove excess water and let it air dry. Avoid using ammonia or a microwave, as they can cause the aluminum to darken.  
User: Got it. It’s dry now. How do I put it back?  
HomeHelper: To re-install, slide the filter back into the frame slot on the left or right, then push it upwards and to the opposite side to lock it in place.

HomeHelper: You're welcome! Remember to clean it every four months to keep it in good condition. Let me know if you need anything else.

scenario: The overheating warning light activates and the vacuum cleaner switches off automatically.
solution_steps:
1. Switch the vacuum cleaner off immediately using the On/Off foot control.
2. Disconnect from the electricity supply. Switch off at the wall socket and unplug it.
3. Remove the cause of overheating, such as large articles blocking the suction tube, a full dustbag, particles of fine dust, or a heavily soiled exhaust or dust compartment filter.
4. Wait for approximately 20-30 minutes to allow the vacuum cleaner to cool down.
5. Once cooled, the vacuum cleaner can be switched on again.

scenario: The dustbag change indicator does not signal when the dustbag is full.
solution_steps:
1. Change the dustbag when the colour marker in the dustbag change indicator turns red, or sooner if it is no longer effective.
2. If a large amount of hair and carpet fluff which typically contains a lot of air is vacuumed up, the indicator may fail to react even though the bag is full. You should still change it.
3. Lift the release catch for the dust compartment lid and raise the lid as far as it will go.
4. Pull the dustbag out by the grip on the collar.
5. Fit the new dustbag into the blue holder as far as it will go. Leave it folded up when you take it out of the box.
6. Dispose of the dustbag when full. Do not attempt to reuse. Blocked pores in used dustbags will reduce the suction power of the vacuum cleaner.

scenario: The vacuum cleaner loses suction power unexpectedly.
solution_steps:
1. "Switch the vacuum cleaner off immediately using the On/Off foot control." Disconnect from the electricity supply. Switch off at the wall socket and unplug it.
2. Check if large articles are blocking the suction tube. Remove any blockages found.
3. Inspect the dustbag to see if it is full or contains particles of fine dust. Replace the dustbag if necessary.

5. After removing the cause, wait for approximately 20 - 30 minutes to allow the vacuum cleaner to cool down. It can then be switched on again.

scenario: The vacuum cleaner fails to start despite being plugged into a power source.
solution_steps:
1. Pull the mains cable out to the required length (max. cable length approx. 7.5 m). Insert the plug into the socket correctly and switch on.

2. Press the On/Off foot control .

3. If the vacuum cleaner still does not start, check if there is an issue with overheating: "A temperature limiter switches the vacuum cleaner off automatically if it gets too hot. This can occur if, for instance, large articles block the suction tube or when the dustbag is full or contains particles of fine dust. A heavily soiled exhaust or dust compartment filter can also be the cause of overheating."

4. If overheating is suspected, switch the vacuum cleaner off immediately using the On/Off foot control . Disconnect from the electricity supply. Switch off at the wall socket and unplug it.

5. After removing the cause of overheating, wait for approximately 20 - 30 minutes to allow the vacuum cleaner to cool down. It can then be switched on again.

scenario: Blockages in the suction hose or tube affect the vacuum cleaner's performance.
solution_steps:
1. Detach the suction hose by pressing the release buttons at the side of the hose connector, and lift the hose from the socket.
2. Check for blockages in the suction hose and remove any obstructions.
3. Connect the suction hose to the handle by inserting the suction hose into the handle until it clicks into position.
4. Connect the handle to the suction tube by inserting the handle into the suction tube until it clicks into position. To do this, line up the guides on the two pieces.
5. To release the handle from the suction tube, press the release button and pull the handle out of the suction tube, twisting it slightly as you do so.
6. Check for blockages in the suction tube and remove any obstructions.
7. Re-connect the suction tube to the handle and ensure it clicks into position.
8. Push the telescopic suction tube into the floorhead/hard floorbrush and turn it clockwise or anti-clockwise until it clicks into position.
9. Check for blockages in the floorhead/hard floorbrush and remove any obstructions.

scenario: Foreign objects causing blockage in the product body or extension pipe.
solution_steps:
1. Remove any foreign objects from inside the product body, extension pipe, inlet port, or nozzle.
2. In order to maintain product performance, be sure to remove any foreign objects and dust from inside the product body, extension pipe, or air inlets.
3. If the inside of the product body, extension pipe, inlets, pre-filter, or fine dust filter is clogged with foreign objects, the power will surge (alternating from Hi to Lo power) a few times to alert you to the blocked airflow. The appliance will then automatically turn off to prevent damage.
4. Separate the battery from the product body and remove the foreign objects before resuming use of the appliance.

scenario: The vacuum is difficult to push due to incorrect height adjustment.
solution_steps:
1. Adjust powerfoot to correct height setting, see page 6.

2. Turn the dial on the foot of the vacuum to the desired setting. If the dial is difficult to turn, tilt the vacuum back slightly to take the weight off the foot while turning.

3. For optimal carpet cleaning performance, adjust to the lowest practical setting. If your vacuum is difficult to push, adjust to the next higher setting.

4. Lowest setting – For low pile carpet or bare floors. To pick up debris, it may be necessary to move up one setting.

5. Medium setting – For medium pile carpet.

6. Highest setting – For high pile and most shag carpet.

scenario: The rotating floor brush is jammed with debris at the brush ends.
solution_steps:
1. Unplug vacuum, turn over and unscrew six (6) Philips head screws to remove the bottom cover. Lift brush straight out.
2. Clean debris from brush roll. Inspect by placing on its end and spin. The brush roll should spin freely, multiple times by one flick. If it doesn’t, replace brush roll.
3. Check belt for wear or cuts and replace if necessary.
4. Replace the brush roll and belt by looping the belt over the motor shaft and the brush roll. Line up the end caps and pull the brush forward into place. This will stretch the belt.
5. Return bottom cover back on and replace the screws.

scenario: Vacuum loses suction power over time, potentially due to clogged filters or blockages.
solution_steps:
1. Check filters to see if they need cleaning. Follow instructions for rinsing and drying the filters before reinserting back into the vacuum. 
2. Dust cup may be full; empty dust cup.
3. Check hose and hose connections for blockages; clear blockages if required.
4. If dust cup is empty, and attachment inlets are clear, check for other blockages.
5. Rotate the suction release collar on the handle clockwise to increase suction power.
6. Ensure that all the filters are clean. Pre-motor filters require washing every 3 months for optimum performance. The post-motor HEPA filter needs to be washed every 2 years.
7. Check intake openings in all accessories.
8. If the vacuum still does not have proper suction, check for blockages in hose, accessories, and inlet openings.

scenario: The polarized plug does not fit into certain outlets, preventing the vacuum from powering on.
solution_steps:
1. To reduce the risk of electric shock, this vacuum cleaner has a polarized plug (one blade is wider than the other).
2. As a safety feature, this plug will fit into a polarized outlet only one way.
3. If the plug does not fit fully into the outlet, reverse the plug.
4. If it still does not fit, contact a qualified electrician. 
5. DO NOT force into outlet or try to modify to fit.

solution_steps:

3. "Wash the filter unit in cold water only: do not use detergent, or wash it in a dishwasher or washing machine."

4. "Wash the pleated paper element of the filter unit first; hold the filter unit under a cold water tap with the foam element downwards and run cold water over the pleated paper."

5. "Continue washing until the water runs clear."

6. "Wash the foam element of the filter unit next; hold the filter unit under a cold water tap with the foam element downwards so that dirty water does not contaminate the pleated paper element. 7. "Continue washing until the water runs clear."

9. "Repeat washing the elements and outside of the filter unit until the water runs clear."

10. "Gently shake the filter unit to remove any excess water and leave to drain with the foam element end facing up."

11. "Leave the filter unit to dry completely in a dry environment with good airflow, for a minimum of 24 hours."

12. "Check that the filter unit is completely dry."

13. "To refit, return the filter unit to the main body and twist clockwise until it clicks into place."

scenario: The machine should not be charged outside of the specified temperature range, which can lead to improper charging.

4. Do not charge the machine and then move it to an area with a temperature below 50°F (10°C) for storage purposes: "Do not charge the machine and then move it to an area with a temperature below 50°F (10°C) for storage purposes."

solution_steps:

3. Do not use vacuum cleaner without dust bag.
4. Keep the airflow passage open. Check the starred areas occasionally for clogs.

scenario: Beater bar does not turn because the Carpet/Bare Floor selector is in the wrong position.
solution_steps:
1. Ensure the vacuum cleaner is in the upright position standing on the handle.

2. Use foot to move pedal to the correct position. As stated, "Selector should be placed in CARPET position when using vacuum cleaner on carpeted floors."

3. Ensure that the "selector should be placed in BARE FLOOR (TOOLS) position when using vacuum cleaner on bare floors and when using tools."

4. Confirm that the beater bar is not automatically stopped. For MC-UL426 model, note: "While operating the vacuum cleaner in the CARPET position, the beater bar will automatically stop rotating when vacuum cleaner is in the upright (locked) position for storage or tool use." Ensure the vacuum is not in the upright (locked) position if using on carpet.

scenario: Motor protection system activated due to clogs.
solution_steps:
1. Turn the vacuum cleaner off and unplug the mains lead from the outlet to allow the vacuum cleaner to cool and the thermal protector to reset.
2. Check for and remove clogs, if necessary (see CLOG REMOVAL, pages 33-34).
3. Also check and clean/replace any clogged filters and empty dust bin, if necessary.
4. Wait approximately fifty (50) minutes and then plug the vacuum cleaner in and turn back on to see if the motor protector has reset.
5. If the bypass valve has opened due to a clog or full dust bin preventing normal air flow, empty dust bin or locate and remove the clog (see CLOG REMOVAL, pages 33-34).
6. Note: The bypass valve may open when cleaning new carpet due to reduced airflow caused by the new carpet lint filling the dust bin quickly.

scenario: Beater bar does not turn due to a worn or broken belt.
solution_steps:
1. Remove the lower plate (See BELT REPLACEMENT, pages 29-31 & 31-32).

2. Remove beater bar by carefully lifting out.

3. Remove worn or broken belt.

4. Loop new belt around motor shaft and beater bar belt groove; see illustration for correct belt routing.

5. Reinstall beater bar back into nozzle housing grooves.

6. After reinstalling the beater bar, turn by hand to make sure that belt is not twisted or pinched and that all rotating parts turn freely.

7. Reinstall lower plate by (1) aligning the tabs on the lower plate with the slots in the nozzle and (2) rotating to installed position. Ensure tabs are locked into slots.

8. Press lower plate onto nozzle and secure by rotating the lower plate latches to the LOCK position.

scenario: Poor job of dirt pick-up due to a full or clogged dust bin.
solution_steps:
1. Turn off and unplug the vacuum cleaner. (page 33)

2. Remove the dust bin from the vacuum cleaner. (page 23)

3. Always empty the dust bin when dirt level reaches the “MAX” line. (page 23)

4. Grasp the handle on the top of the dust bin. Lift up and out to remove the dust bin from the vacuum cleaner. (page 23)

5. Press the dust bin release button to open the dust bin door. The debris will fall out. (page 24)

6. Remove any clogs that might be located in the pre-filter. (page 24)

7. After the dust bin is empty of debris, firmly close the door. Make sure you hear a “click” sound to indicate that the door is fully latched. (page 24)

8. Place the dust bin back into the vacuum cleaner by inserting the bottom first and tilting back. Push forward until the dust bin locks in place. (page 24)

scenario: Poor job of dirt pick-up because of a dirty pre-filter, primary filter, and/or exhaust filter.
solution_steps:
1. Turn off and unplug the vacuum cleaner.
2. Remove dust bin (See EMPTYING DUST BIN, pages 23-24).
3. Pull the dust bin lid latch and open the dust bin lid.
4. Remove the primary filter.
5. Wash with cold water only, DO NOT use detergent or soap.
6. Once the filter is washed clean, squeeze by hand and allow to air dry. Allow filter to dry for 24 hours before placing back into vacuum cleaner. DO NOT install damp.
7. Place the primary filter into the dust bin lid.
8. Close the dust bin lid. Be sure the dust bin lid latch snaps in place. A noticeable “click” should be heard.
9. Reinstall the dust bin into the vacuum cleaner (See EMPTYING DUST BIN, pages 23-24).
10. Turn off and unplug the vacuum cleaner.
11. Press latch to remove exhaust filter cover.
12. Grasp the exhaust filter and pull out to remove.
13. Place the new exhaust filter into the vacuum cleaner with the AIRFLOW arrow pointing upwards.
14. Reinstall the exhaust filter cover by inserting the tab into the slot in the vacuum cleaner. Press firmly to snap exhaust filter cover into place.

scenario: A burning smell is detected, and the brush roll will not turn, indicating debris in the brush roll or a broken belt.
solution_steps:
1. Check brushroll for debris.
2. Step on handle release and lay vacuum cleaner face down.
3. Use Phillips screwdriver to remove 6 screws from brushroll cover.
4. Lift off cover.
5. Rotate right end of brushroll and lift out.
6. Lift out left end of brushroll.
7. Replace broken or out of shape belt.
8. Position new belt around motor shaft.
9. Loop new belt around brushroll shaft at left end of brushroll.
10. To reposition brushroll into base, pull belt down and insert left end of brushroll first. Align brushroll end cap with slot so it fits into position.
11. Press right end of brushroll into position.
12. Align slot on cover with tab and snap cover into place.
13. Replace 6 screws.

scenario: The vacuum cleaner does not clean floors effectively, potentially due to a full dust cup, or clogged filters.
solution_steps:
1. Empty dust cup after every use. Press release button and lift off dust cup. Hold dust cup over wastebasket and press lever to release bottom lid. Debris will empty.

2. Clean and/or change filter. Washable dust cup filters – Clean monthly. Pull dust cup latch to lift up dust cup lid. Lift out foam filter and shake off dust. Rinse foam filter and dry THOROUGHLY.

3. Align tab on filter screen with slot on back of dust cup and drop into position. Grip tabs and lift out filter screen. Twist bottom of filter screen counterclockwise to unlock and pull apart. Shake off dust. Rinse screen and dust cup. Dry all THOROUGHLY. Reassemble screen; twist clockwise to lock.

4. Reinstall foam filter, filter screen, and dust cup in proper position. Close cover until it clicks.

5. Check vacuum height adjustment knob position.

6. Clean brushroll if needed. Check brushroll for debris. Replace broken or out of shape belt if necessary.

scenario: Overheating of the TV due to blocked ventilation holes.
solution_steps:
1. Prevent TV from overheating by placing in an area with good ventilation.
2. Do not block ventilation holes on the TV. Position the TV so air can circulate freely on all sides.
3. Do not stack objects on the TV.
4. If you place the TV on a stand, make sure you allow adequate ventilation.
5. Do not allow any of the apparatus’ ventilation openings to be blocked by objects that might obstruct them, such as newspapers, curtains, tablecloths, or any other objects. 
6. Do not expose the apparatus to any external heat sources.
7. Do not place any heat sources such as candles, lamps, etc. on the apparatus.
