scenario: The Wall-Mount Bracket may fall if the supplied screws and anchors are not used, potentially causing injury or property damage.
solution_steps:
1. Be sure to subcontract the installation to licensed contractors and keep small children away during the installation.

2. Use a level to check whether the Wall-Mount Bracket is level.

3. The wall should be capable of supporting a weight of at least six times the TV or LCD Display weight. (Refer to your TV’s or LCD Display’s “Reference Guide” for its weight.)

4. Make sure to attach the Table-Top stand before installing the TV or LCD Display to the wall by referring to the Setup Guide.

5. Remove the screws from the rear of the TV or LCD Display. Be sure to store the removed screws and unused parts in a safe place, keeping them away from children.

6. Attach the Wall-Mount Attachment (supplied with the TV or LCD Display) to the rear of the TV or LCD Display (to make it parallel with the wall).

7. If the installation of the Wall-Mount Bracket on the wall is not sufficiently sturdy, the unit may fall and cause injury or property damage.

scenario: Inadequate support from the wall material may cause the Wall-Mount Bracket to fail.
solution_steps:
1. Firstly, check the type of the wall to install the TV or LCD Display. The Wall-Mount Bracket differs depending on the type of the wall.

2. For dry wall with studs: 
   - Maximum dry wall thickness: 16 mm (5/8 inch).
   - Ensure that the inner wood stud size is at least 51 x 102 mm (2 x 4 inch) for common or 38 x 89 mm (1 1/2 x 3 1/2 inch) for nominal.
   - Keep minimum 406 mm (16 inch) horizontal space between fasteners.
   - Use the Lateral Shift Bracket.

3. For solid concrete or concrete block:
   - Mount the Wall-Mount Bracket directly onto the solid concrete wall.
   - Ensure that the thickness of solid concrete wall is at least 203 mm (8 inch).
   - Ensure that the size of each concrete block is at least 203 x 203 x 406 mm (8 x 8 x 16 inch).
   - Use the Wall-Mount Bracket. 

4. Use a level to check whether WM1 is level when aligning to the wall and when installing on the wall.

5. Do not over-tighten the lag bolts WS2. Improper tightening could reduce the holding power of the lag bolts WS2.

scenario: "Weak or No Signal" is displayed in TV mode or channels cannot be found.
solution_steps:
1. Make sure that the external device is connected securely and turned on. Move to Connected Devices to switch to other input sources.
2. When using a set-top box or cable box, check the broadcast signals or the network that is connected to the external device.
3. Confirm that the coaxial cable is securely connected to the TV.
4. Run Factory data reset or Auto Tuning.
   - left directional button Settings All Settings General & Privacy Factory data reset Try Now
   - left directional button Settings All Settings General & Privacy Broadcasting (Auto Tuning Settings) Auto Tuning Try Now
5. If your TV is not connected to a cable box or satellite box, run Auto Tuning.
   - left directional button Settings All Settings General & Privacy Broadcasting (Auto Tuning Settings) Auto Tuning Try Now
6. When using a broadcast receiver such as set-top box and IPTV, check the connection to the TV.
   - left directional button Connected Devices Connection Guide Try Now
7. When the symptom persists, contact your service provider.

5. For detailed instructions on connecting to Wireless One Connect, launch Connection Guide.
   - Use the left directional button to go to Connected Devices > Connection Guide > Wireless One Connect.

scenario: The video is okay but there is no audio when using external devices.
solution_steps:
1. If you are using an HDMI connection, check the audio output setting on your PC.
2. If you are using a DVI to HDMI cable, a separate audio cable is required.
3. To listen to the computer sound, connect external speakers to the audio output connection of the computer.
4. Check the Sound Output setting. If it is set to TV Speaker, check the volume setting.
5. If you are using an external device, check the device’s audio output option. For example, you may need to change your cable box’s audio option to HDMI if the box connected to your TV is using an HDMI cable.
6. To listen to computer sound, connect an external speaker to the computer’s audio output connector.
7. If your TV has a headphone jack, make sure there is nothing plugged into it.
8. Reboot the connected device by disconnecting and then reconnecting the device’s power cord.
9. With a set-top box or cable box, check the cable connection and reboot the external device. When the symptom persists, contact your service provider.

scenario: There is a failure to connect to a wireless network or access point.
solution_steps:
1. Ensure that the network cable is connected and the router is powered on.
2. Connect your mobile device to the router via Wi-Fi.
3. Turn the router off and back on again. (Requires 2 to 3 minutes)
4. If a security key is required, make sure it has been entered correctly.
5. Unplug the TV’s power cord and plug it back in or press and hold the power button for at least 3 seconds.
6. Make sure that there is no electromagnetic wave generating device placed between the TV and router.
7. If unable to establish a wireless internet connection, connect the TV to the wireless router via a LAN cable.
8. If the TV is able to connect to the internet normally via the cable connection, there might be a problem with the wireless router. In this case, try using a different wireless router.

scenario: There is no picture/video on the screen.
solution_steps:

2. Set your external devices’ (Cable/Set top Box, DVD, Blu-ray etc) video outputs to match the connections to the TV input. For example, if an external device’s output is HDMI, it should be connected to an HDMI input on the TV.
3. Make sure your connected devices are powered on.
4. Be sure to select the TV’s correct source by pressing the SOURCE button on the TV remote.
5. Reboot the connected device by reconnecting the device’s power cable.

scenario: The TV picture quality is poor, and the test image is not displayed properly during the Picture Test.
solution_steps:
1. If the test image is not properly displayed, ensure that your TV is receiving a good quality signal from the source or signal.
2. Check the connection type you are using. If you have an analogue cable/set top box, upgrade to a digital set top box. Use HDMI or Component cables to deliver HD (high definition) picture quality.
3. If you are a Cable/Satellite subscriber, try digital stations from the channel line up.
4. If you are using an Aerial connection, try HD stations after performing Auto tuning.
5. If the picture size is set to Screen Fit, change it to 16:9.
6. Change the cable/satellite box resolution.
7. Adjust the Picture options in the TV menu. (go to Picture Mode / Colour / Brightness / Sharpness)
8. Adjust Energy Saving option in the TV menu. (go to MENU - System - Eco Solution - Energy Saving)
9. Try resetting the picture to view the default picture settings. (go to MENU - Picture - Reset Picture)

scenario: The message “This file may not be playable properly.” appears due to high bit rate content.
solution_steps:
1. The message “This file may not be playable properly.” appears because of high bit rate of content. Content generally will play but could experience some playability issue.
2. To address potential playability issues, ensure that the video content's standard bit rate/frame rate does not exceed the compatible Frame/sec listed in the table from the manual.
3. Sound or video may not work if the contents have a standard bit rate/frame rate above the compatible Frame/sec listed in the table.
4. Check if the video content or container has an error; video content will not play, or not play correctly, if there is an error in the content or the container.
5. If the Index Table is in error, the Seek (Jump) function is not supported.

scenario: Media server software compatibility issues with the TV, preventing media sharing.
solution_steps:
1. Install media server software on your computer. Use a recent version of media server software like Windows Media Player 11, Twonky™ or similar.

2. Set up the media server software to share your media files with the TV. Read the manual of the media server software for more information.

3. Ensure that the media server software is running on your computer to open your files on the TV.

4. Follow these steps to ensure your TV is set up correctly:
   - Press h and select S Setup and press OK.
   - Select Network settings and press OK.
   - Select Digital Media Renderer - DMR and press OK.
   - Select On and press OK.
   - Press b, repeatedly if necessary, to close the menu.

5. Make sure that the router of your wireless network is switched on.

6. If needed, in the Help section, press List and look up Media server software, supported for an overview of supported media server software.

4. If the antenna reception is poor, use a highly directional outdoor antenna (if applicable).
5. If the station may have broadcast difficulties, try another channel.
6. To view the antenna or Cable signal: Select the ANT/CABLE video input source on the TV.

scenario: Problems arising from the appliance being walked on or pinched power cords.
solution_steps:
1) Protect the power cord from being walked on or pinched, particularly at plugs, convenience receptacles, and the point where they exit from the apparatus.

2) If the power-supply cord or plug is damaged, refer all servicing to qualified service personnel. Servicing is required when the apparatus has been damaged in any way.

3) ALWAYS unplug the TV to completely disconnect from mains power. When the TV is turned off using the on/off switch, it is not completely disconnected from power and a minute amount of current is still consumed.

4) If the TV does not operate normally, take the following precautions: ALWAYS turn off the TV and unplug the power cord to avoid possible electric shock or fire.

scenario: Refrigerator compartment remains open, triggering an alarm.
solution_steps:

3. The warning sound is switched off and the alarm off button no longer flashes.

   - Press the A/Y Settings button until settings display shows On or OF.
   - Press the menu button.
   - The setting is saved.

scenario: Refrigerator rocks and is not stable, suggesting the need for leveling adjustments.
solution_steps:
1. Move the refrigerator into its final location. If necessary, open both doors to 90° and remove the base grille.

2. The two leveling feet are located on the brackets on each side of the product.

3. Use a ¹⁄₄" open-ended or adjustable wrench to adjust the leveling feet. Turn the leveling foot to the left to raise that side of the product, or turn it to the right to lower that side of the product.

4. Open both doors again and check that they close as easily as you like. If not, tilt the refrigerator slightly more to the rear by turning the leveling feet to the left. It may take several more turns, and you should turn both leveling feet the same amount.

5. Use a bubble level to check the leveling of the refrigerator.

6. Whenever you need to move the refrigerator, turn the leveling feet to the right until they are no longer touching the ground. This will allow the refrigerator to roll more easily.

scenario: Ice maker is not producing ice, implying potential issues with ice production mechanisms.
solution_steps:
1. Refrigerator is not connected to a water supply, or the water supply shutoff valve is not fully turned on - Connect the refrigerator to a water supply and make sure the water shutoff valve is fully open.
2. Kink in the water source line - A kink in the water line can reduce water flow, resulting in decreased ice production, small ice cubes, and/or hollow or irregularly-shaped ice. Straighten the water line.
3. Ice maker is not turned on - Turn on the ice maker. See “Ice Maker and Storage Bin.”
4. New installation - After connecting the refrigerator to a water source, flush the water system. (See “Water and Ice Dispensers.”) Wait 24 hours for ice production to begin. Wait 72 hours for full ice production.
5. Large amount of ice was recently removed - Allow sufficient time for the ice maker to produce more ice.
6. Ice is jammed in the ice maker ejector arm - Remove ice from the ejector arm using a plastic utensil.
7. Inadequate water pressure - Verify that the household has adequate water pressure. See “Water Supply Requirements.”
8. Water filter is installed incorrectly - Make sure the filter is properly installed. See “Water Filtration System.”
9. A reverse osmosis water filtration system is connected to your cold water supply - This can decrease water pressure. See “Water Supply Requirements.”

scenario: Ice maker is not producing ice, implying potential issues with ice production mechanisms.
solution_steps:
1. Refrigerator is not connected to a water supply, or the water supply shutoff valve is not fully turned on - Connect the refrigerator to a water supply and make sure the water shutoff valve is fully open.
2. Kink in the water source line - A kink in the water line can reduce water flow, resulting in decreased ice production, small ice cubes, and/or hollow or irregularly-shaped ice. Straighten the water line.
3. Ice maker is not turned on - Turn on the ice maker. See “Ice Maker and Storage Bin.”
4. New installation - After connecting the refrigerator to a water source, flush the water system. (See “Water and Ice Dispensers.”) Wait 24 hours for ice production to begin. Wait 72 hours for full ice production.
5. Large amount of ice was recently removed - Allow sufficient time for the ice maker to produce more ice.
6. Ice is jammed in the ice maker ejector arm - Remove ice from the ejector arm using a plastic utensil.
7. Inadequate water pressure - Verify that the household has adequate water pressure. See “Water Supply Requirements.”
8. Water filter is installed incorrectly - Make sure the filter is properly installed. See “Water Filtration System.”
9. A reverse osmosis water filtration system is connected to your cold water supply - This can decrease water pressure. See “Water Supply Requirements.”

scenario: Trouble connecting the appliance to a Wi-Fi network if the wireless network name (SSID) is set incorrectly.
solution_steps:
1. Verify that the wireless network name (SSID) is set correctly. The wireless network name (SSID) should be a combination of English letters and numbers. Do not use special characters.

2. If the security protocol of the router is set to WEP, change the security protocol to WPA2, which is recommended, and connect the product again.

3. Ensure that the router frequency is set to 2.4 GHz. Only a 2.4 GHz router frequency is supported. To check the router frequency, contact your Internet service provider or refer to your wireless router manual.

4. If the firewall on your wireless router is enabled, disable the firewall or add an exception to it.

5. If the appliance is too far from the router, the signal may be weak and the connection may not be configured correctly. Move the router closer to the appliance or purchase and install a Wi-Fi repeater.

6. If the network connection may not work properly depending on the Internet service provider, check with them for any issues.

7. If the appliance cannot be connected due to problems with the wireless signal transmission, unplug the appliance and wait about a minute before trying again.

scenario: Refrigerator is not leveled properly, affecting door alignment and operation.
solution_steps:
1. Turn the leveling leg to the left to raise that side of the refrigerator or to the right to lower it. It may take several turns of the leveling leg to adjust the tilt of the refrigerator. A flare nut wrench works best, but an open-end wrench will suffice. Do not over-tighten.

2. Open both doors and check to make sure that they close easily. If the doors do not close easily, tilt the refrigerator slightly more to the rear by turning both leveling legs to the left. It may take several more turns, and be sure to turn both leveling legs the same amount.

3. Both the left and right refrigerator doors have an adjustable nut, located on the bottom hinge, to raise and lower them to align properly. If the space between the doors is uneven, use the wrench (included with the owner's manual) to turn the nut in the door hinge to adjust the height.

4. Open the door and use the wrench to loosen the keeper nut by turning it to the left.

scenario: Audible diagnosis is interrupted if the phone is not correctly placed near the refrigerator's speaker.
solution_steps:

2. Open the right refrigerator door.
3. Hold the Lock button for three seconds. If the display has been locked for over five minutes, you must deactivate the lock and then reactivate it.
4. Hold the mouthpiece of your phone in front of the speaker that is located on the right hinge of the refrigerator door.
5. Press and hold the Freezer button for three seconds while continuing to hold your phone to the speaker.
6. After you hear three beeps, release the Freezer button.
7. Keep the phone in place until the tone transmission has finished. The display will count down the time. Once the countdown is over and the tones have stopped, the diagnosis will be displayed in the application.
8. For best results, do not move the phone while the tones are being transmitted.

scenario: Doors are often opened or left open for long periods, impacting the refrigerator's ability to maintain the set temperature.
solution_steps:
1. To lessen the effect of moisture buildup, reduce the frequency and duration of door openings. 
2. When the doors are opened often or for long periods of time, warm, humid air enters the compartment. This raises the temperature and moisture level within the compartment.
3. Adding food and opening the door warms the refrigerator, requiring the compressor to run longer in order to cool the refrigerator back down. 
4. In order to conserve energy, try to get everything you need out of the refrigerator at once, keep food organized so it is easy to find, and close the door as soon as the food is removed. (Refer to the Food Storage Guide.)
5. Firmly push the doors shut. If they will not shut all the way, see the "Doors will not close correctly or pop open" section in Troubleshooting.

scenario: The SmartThings app fails to operate specifically with Samsung Smart Home models.
solution_steps:
1. Ensure that the SmartThings app is available for applicable models only.
2. Verify that you are not attempting to connect using the old Samsung Smart Refrigerator app, as it cannot connect with Samsung Smart Home models.
3. You must log into your Samsung account to use the app.
4. Make sure that your router is operating normally.
5. If the Wi-Fi icon on the refrigerator’s display is off, this indicates that no network connection has been established. Use the SmartThings app to connect and register your refrigerator to the access point (AP) of your house.
6. If the SmartThings app is successfully connected to your refrigerator but does not run, exit and restart the SmartThings app, or disconnect and reconnect the router.
7. Power off the refrigerator, and then power it on again after 1 minute.

scenario: Water flow is weaker than normal due to low water pressure in the connected supply.
solution_steps:
1. Make sure the water pressure is between 206-861 kPa.
2. If the water pressure is below these specifications, check if the sediment filter in the reverse osmosis system is blocked. Replace the filter if necessary.
3. Refill the water tank in the reverse osmosis system with water.
4. If your refrigerator has a water filter, it may further reduce the water pressure when used in conjunction with a reverse osmosis system. Remove the water filter.
5. For more information or servicing, contact a licensed plumbing professional.

1. Replace fuse or reset the breaker.
2. Have the wall outlet and circuit checked by a qualified electrician to make sure the outlet is properly grounded.
3. The refrigerator should always be plugged into its own individual electrical outlet which has a voltage rating that matches the rating plate.
4. Plug into a grounded 3-prong outlet.
conversation:

User: I haven't checked that yet. How do I know if there's power?

HomeHelper: A simple way is to plug in another device, like a lamp, to see if it turns on. If it doesn't, the outlet might not have power.

User: Okay, I tried that, and the lamp didn't turn on. What does that mean?

HomeHelper: It sounds like there might be an issue with the power supply to the outlet. Have you checked your home's fuse box or circuit breaker panel?

HomeHelper: Look for any tripped breakers or blown fuses. If you find one, reset the breaker or replace the fuse, and then check the outlet again.

User: I found a tripped breaker and reset it. The lamp works now! Should I plug the fridge back in?

HomeHelper: Great! Yes, you can plug the fridge back in. Make sure it's plugged into its own dedicated outlet that matches the voltage rating on the fridge's rating plate.

User: It's plugged in now, but the light still isn't working. What else could be wrong?

HomeHelper: Since there's power, it's possible the outlet isn't properly grounded. It might be best to have a qualified electrician check the outlet and circuit for proper grounding.

User: That sounds a bit complicated. Is it really necessary?

HomeHelper: Proper grounding is important for safety and to ensure your fridge functions correctly. An electrician can confirm everything is set up safely.

HomeHelper: Just make sure the fridge is plugged into a grounded 3-prong outlet. Once the electrician checks everything, you should be good to go!

User: Got it. Thanks for your help! I feel a bit more at ease now.

HomeHelper: You're welcome! I'm glad I could help. Don't hesitate to reach out if you have more questions.

scenario: The SmartThings app fails to connect to the refrigerator for remote control.
solution_steps:

2. Verify that your router is operating normally: "Make sure that your router is operating normally."

3. Check that the Wi-Fi icon on the refrigerator's display is on. If it is off, it indicates that no network connection has been established yet: "If the Wi-Fi icon on the refrigerator’s display is off, this indicates that no network connection has been established yet."

4. Use the SmartThings app to connect and register your refrigerator to the access point (AP) of your house: "In this case, use the SmartThings app to connect and register your refrigerator to the access point (AP) of your house."

5. If the connection fails due to distance from your access point or electrical interference, wait a moment and try again: "Easy Connection may fail due to the distance from your access point (AP) or electrical interference from the surrounding environment. Wait a moment and try again."

6. Exit and restart the SmartThings app, or disconnect and reconnect the router if the app is successfully connected but does not run: "Exit and restart the SmartThings app, or disconnect and reconnect the router."

scenario: Abnormal sounds are heard from the refrigerator during operation.
solution_steps:
1. Review the checkpoints in the manual to determine if the sounds you are hearing are considered normal. The manual states: "Any service calls related to normal sounds will be charged to the user."
2. Check if the sounds are similar to a car engine igniting when starting or ending an operation. The manual notes that "As the operation stabilizes, the sounds will decrease."
3. Listen for clicking, chirping, or buzzing sounds while the fan is operating. The manual mentions that "When the refrigerator reaches the set temperature, no fan sound will occur."
4. During a defrost cycle, pay attention to any sizzling sounds. The manual explains that "water may drip on the defrost heater, causing sizzling sounds."
5. Identify if bubbling sounds occur. According to the manual, "as the refrigerator cools or freezes, refrigerant gas moves through sealed pipes, causing bubbling sounds."
6. Notice any knocking noises as the refrigerator temperature changes. The manual indicates that "plastic parts contract and expand, creating knocking noises" during the defrosting cycle or when electronic parts are working.
7. For ice maker models, check for buzzing sounds when the water valve opens to fill the ice maker.
8. Be aware of whooshing sounds when opening and closing the refrigerator door. The manual states that "because of pressure equalizing," these sounds may occur.

scenario: The Power Freeze function does not activate or indicate when in use.
solution_steps:
1. Ensure that the freezer is not set to Off mode, as the Power Freeze function cannot be activated if the freezer is off. The manual states, "When the freezer is set to Off mode, the freezer temperature will be kept under 15 °C, but the fridge remains active as previously set."

2. Check the freezer indicator on the main panel to see if the Power Freeze function is indicated. The manual mentions, "• indicates that the Power Freeze function is on."

3. If the Power Freeze function is not indicated, verify that you have selected the correct compartment and confirmed your selection. The manual states, "Wait for 5 seconds to confirm your selection. - The selected compartment’s indicator stops blinking."

4. Remember that the appearance of the main panel may differ from the figure in the manual, as stated, "The actual appearance of your main panel may differ from the figure and the main panel design is subject to change without notice."

5. If the Power Freeze function remains unresponsive, consider checking the AI Energy Mode. The manual suggests, "The icon appears when the AI Energy Mode is operating. You may turn on or off the AI Energy Mode in the SmartThings app. (applicable models only)". This may affect the operation of the Power Freeze function.

6. If none of the above steps resolve the issue, verify if the increased power consumption from using Power Freeze is a factor. The manual notes, "Using Power Cool or Power Freeze increases power consumption." Ensure your appliance is properly powered and not experiencing any power issues.

scenario: The freezer does not maintain the set temperature accurately.
solution_steps:
1. Properly plug in the power cord.
2. Set the temperature lower.
3. Keep the refrigerator away from direct sunlight or a heat source.
4. We recommend that the gap between the refrigerator and nearby walls (or cabinets) is more than 50 mm.
5. Ensure that food is not blocking the refrigerator.
6. Activate Power Freeze for at least 20 hours before putting food in the freezer to freeze large amounts of food.

scenario: The Peak Demand indicator does not display the correct status of the Peak Demand function.
solution_steps:

3. If the refrigerator receives a SMART GRID (Demand Response) signal from the utility company, 'Or' is displayed in the freezer temperature display.
4. Alternatively, you can activate or deactivate Peak Demand Off (Override mode) using the SmartThings app and the Energy Management function.
5. Ensure the corresponding app is installed to use the Energy Management refrigerator functions.

1. Fully open the corresponding door.
2. Hold the front of the shelf, and then gently lift up and pull out. Note: Do not lift up the shelf fully when removing or reinserting the shelf. The rear wall of the fridge room can be dented.
3. To reinsert, hold the shelf at an angle so the front is higher than the back, and then insert the top hook into the top shelf notch.
4. Lower the shelf and insert the bottom shelf hook into the bottom shelf notch. Caution: The tempered glass shelves are heavy. Use caution when removing them. The shelf must be inserted correctly. Do not insert upside down. Glass containers may scratch the surface of glass shelves.

scenario: Ice crushing function does not crush ice effectively, resulting in large chunks remaining.
solution_steps:
1. Use the PULSE button to begin the blending process when preparing beverages that include ice cubes; this helps to produce a smoother texture.
2. When using PULSE function use short bursts. Allow the blades to stop rotating between pulses. Do not use pulse for more than 2 minutes.
3. It is helpful to begin the blending process on the lowest speed and then increase to a higher speed, if necessary.
4. Make sure to scrape down sides on blending jar, if necessary, and continue blending.
5. Do not run blender for longer than 30 seconds when using dry foods and 2 minutes when blending liquids.
conversation:
User: Hi, I'm having trouble with my blender's ice crushing function. It leaves big chunks instead of crushing them properly.

HomeHelper: I understand how frustrating that can be. Let's try a few things to improve the ice crushing. Have you tried using the PULSE button to start the blending process?

User: I haven't used the PULSE button much. How does that help?

HomeHelper: The PULSE function helps to create a smoother texture by using short bursts. It’s important to let the blades stop rotating between each pulse. Have you tried that?

User: No, I usually just keep it running. Should I pulse for a long time?

HomeHelper: It's best to use the PULSE function in short bursts and not for more than 2 minutes. This should help with the ice crushing.

User: Okay, I'll try that. Should I start with a high speed?

HomeHelper: Actually, it's better to begin on the lowest speed and then increase to a higher speed if needed. This gradual increase can help with smoother blending.

User: Got it. What if the ice still sticks to the sides of the jar?

scenario: Cheese does not shred well, which may be related to incorrect processing techniques or settings.
solution_steps:

3. Verify that you are using the reversible slicing/shredding disc correctly. The manual instructs, "The reversible slicing/shredding disc has a slicing blade on one side and shredding teeth on the other. The name stamped on the blade, facing up, is the function selected. 4. Make sure you are using the recommended food size and quantity to be processed. The manual advises to "Refer to the Food Processing Charts for recommended food sizes and speeds."

5. Check if the bowl and lid are locked in place as they "may have moved slightly during processing." See “How to Use” sections for further guidance.

scenario: Vegetables are not shredding or slicing as expected, which could be due to incorrect food size or quantity.
solution_steps:
1. Check if the bowl and lid are locked in place as they may have moved slightly during processing. Refer to the "How to Use" sections.
2. Ensure that the processed food is not packed too much in the food chute or pushed too hard with the food pusher, as it may cause the food to be irregularly sliced or shredded. Refer to the Food Processing Charts for recommended sizes and quantities.
3. Verify that the disc attachments are reversible and labeled. The label should face up for the desired function. When using disc attachments, do not process past the MAX LEVEL on the bowl.
4. Make sure to use the Reversible Slicing/Shredding Disc with the desired cutting edge facing up, depending on whether you want to slice or shred.

2. If the plug or cord requires replacing a new cord set should be fitted by an Authorised Kenwood Repairer.
3. For non-rewireable plugs the fuse cover MUST be refitted when replacing the fuse. If the fuse cover is lost then the plug must not be used until a replacement can be obtained. The correct fuse cover is identified by colour and a replacement may be obtained from your Kenwood Authorised Repairer.
4. If a non-rewireable plug is cut off it must be DESTROYED IMMEDIATELY. An electric shock hazard may arise if an unwanted non-rewireable plug is inadvertently inserted into a socket outlet.
5. If you need help with servicing, spare parts or repairs (in or out of guarantee), call Kenwood customer care on 0345 222 0458 in the UK. Have your model number (e.g. TYPE: FDP65) and date code (5 digit code e.g. 21T04) ready. They are on the underside of the power unit.
6. For other countries, if you experience any problems with the operation of your appliance, before requesting assistance refer to the ‘Troubleshooting Guide’ section in the manual or visit www.kenwoodworld.com.

scenario: The mini chopper/mill attachment may draw the maximum load, causing the appliance to overheat if used improperly.
solution_steps:

3 Turn the blade assembly upside down. Lower it into the jar, blades down.
4 Screw the blade assembly onto the jar until finger tight. Refer to the graphics on the underside of the blade assembly as follows: - Unlocked position - Locked position.
5 Place the mill onto the power unit and turn clockwise to lock in position.
6 Select Maximum speed or use the pulse (P).
7 Never fit the blade assembly to the power unit without the jar/lid fitted.
8 Never unscrew the jar/lid while the mill is fitted to your appliance.
9 Do not touch the sharp blades – Keep the blade assembly away from children.
10 Never remove the mill until the blades have completely stopped.
11 Do not process hot ingredients in the mill; allow to cool down to room temperature before processing.

scenario: Blender overheats and shuts off due to Automatic Overload Protection when blending at low speed for too long.
solution_steps:
1. Refer to the tip in the manual: "Blending too long at too low a speed setting will overheat the machine and cause the Automatic Overload Protection to turn the machine off." To prevent overheating, use the High speed as often as possible to achieve the most uniform consistency and maximize the motor’s cooling fan.

2. If the Automatic Overload Protection is activated and the blender shuts off, the manual states: "When engaged, this Automatic Overload Protection will cause the motor to shut off and possibly emit a light odor." 

3. To reset your machine after Automatic Overload Protection is activated, refer to the manual: "If your Automatic Overload Protection should ever be activated, refer to page 7 in this manual to easily reset your machine."

4. To prevent "overloading" your Vitamix machine in the future, follow these additional tips from the manual:
   - "Process only Vitamix recipes when learning to use the machine."
   - "Do not process recipes at lower speeds than recommended."
   - "Do not process recipes longer than recommended."
   - "Use your tamper to process thicker mixtures and keep ingredients moving around and through the blades."

scenario: Risk of burns or scalding when blending hot liquids or ingredients without proper precautions.

6. Lock the lid. This will prevent expansion from affecting the position of the lid when the machine is turned on.

8. Always operate the blender with lid and lid plug firmly in place. The lid plug should be removed only when adding ingredients and when using the tamper.

scenario: The container cover does not securely lock in place, preventing the appliance from operating.
solution_steps:
1. Align the base and bowl as illustrated in Figure 1. Align the bowl handle with the UNLOCK mark on the base. Turn the bowl counter-clockwise until it clicks onto the base. The bowl handle should now align with the LOCK mark on the base. The bowl handle will be positioned above the control buttons. There is only one position for the bowl to lock onto the base. The unit will not operate if the bowl does not lock onto the base.

2. Place the cover onto the bowl. Align the UNLOCK mark on the cover and the UNLOCK mark on the bowl as illustrated in Figure 2. Twist the cover counter-clockwise towards the LOCK until it clicks onto the bowl. The LOCK mark on the cover should now align with the LOCK mark on the bowl. 

3. Ensure that when the cover is locked into position, the safety mechanism on the cover and bowl align. The unit will not operate if the cover is not locked onto the bowl. 

4. Confirm that the bowl is locked into the base before attempting to lock the cover into position.

scenario: The appliance fails to operate when the container is not correctly positioned on the motor base.
solution_steps:
1. Align the base and bowl as illustrated in Figure 1. Align the bowl handle with the UNLOCK mark on the base. Turn the bowl counter-clockwise until it clicks onto the base. The bowl handle should now align with the LOCK mark on the base. (The bowl handle will be positioned above the control buttons).

2. Note: There is only one position for the bowl to lock onto the base. The unit will not operate if the bowl does not lock onto the base.

3. Place the cover onto the bowl. Align the UNLOCK mark on the cover and the UNLOCK mark on the bowl (as illustrated in Figure 2). Twist the cover counter-clockwise towards the LOCK until it clicks onto the bowl. The LOCK mark on the cover should now align with the LOCK mark on the bowl.

4. Note: When the cover is locked into position, the safety mechanism on the cover and bowl will align. The unit will not operate if the cover is not locked onto the bowl.

2. 3. Ensure that the processing bowl, lid, and large pusher are correctly assembled before operating the appliance to engage the safety interlock and allow the motor to run. (Refer to OPERATION section: "The food processor will only operate when the processing bowl, lid and large pusher are correctly assembled. HomeHelper: Of course! It's important to process your ingredients in batches to avoid overloading. Start by placing all your ingredients in the bowl, beginning with the liquids. Just be careful not to exceed the MAX LIQUID level marked on your bowl.

User: Okay, I think I can do that. But how do I actually process them without messing it up?

HomeHelper: Great question! Use the PULSE button to process your ingredients. This helps fold them evenly without over-processing. Just give it a few pulses until everything looks well combined.

User: I see. But what if I accidentally over-process? I'm really worried about that.

HomeHelper: No worries! Just keep an eye on the texture. You want everything to be mixed but not too smooth. If you notice the mixture getting too fine, stop pulsing.

User: Got it. And what if the ingredients stick to the sides of the bowl?

HomeHelper: If that happens, simply scrape down the sides of the bowl as needed during processing. This ensures everything gets mixed evenly.

User: That makes sense. What if I'm processing a smaller amount of ingredients?

HomeHelper: For smaller quantities, place the items to the far left in the feed chute. Alternatively, you can use the small feed chute if the food size allows for it. This helps with even processing.

HomeHelper: Always remember to place the spindle and dough blade into the processing bowl before adding any food. This setup is crucial for proper processing.

scenario: The appliance does not turn on even when plugged in.
solution_steps:
1. Make sure the work bowl and work bowl cover are properly locked on the base.

2. See if the Food Processor is plugged into a proper electrical outlet. If it is, unplug the Food Processor, then plug it into the same outlet again.

3. If the Food Processor still does not work, check the fuse or circuit breaker on the electrical circuit the Food Processor is connected to and make sure the circuit is closed.

4. If the problem cannot be corrected with the steps in this section, see the KitchenAid Warranty and Service section on pages 53-54. Do not return the Food Processor to the retailer – they do not provide service.

scenario: The food processor vibrates excessively when processing food.
solution_steps:
1. Never process any food that is so hard or firmly frozen that it cannot be pierced with the tip of a sharp knife. Hard food can cause damage to the blade or motor. If a piece of hard food, such as carrot, becomes wedged or stuck on the blade, stop the processor and remove the blade. Carefully remove food from the blade.

2. Do not overfill work bowl or mini bowl. For thin mixtures, fill work bowl up to 1⁄2 to 2⁄3 full. For thicker mixtures, fill work bowl up to 3⁄4 full. For liquids, fill up to the maximum level as described on page 10. When chopping, the work bowl should be no more than 1⁄3 to 1⁄2 full. Use the mini bowl for up to 1 cup of liquid or 1⁄2 cup solids.

3. Ensure that the work bowl and work bowl cover are properly locked on the base.

4. Make sure the Food Processor is plugged into a proper electrical outlet. If it is, unplug the Food Processor, then plug it into the same outlet again. If the Food Processor still does not work, check the fuse or circuit breaker on the electrical circuit the Food Processor is connected to and make sure the circuit is closed.

4. After removing the work bowl cover, place it upside down on the counter. This will help keep the counter clean.
5. If any plastic parts should discolor due to the types of food processed, clean them with lemon juice.

scenario: FP3-2 system leaks when connected to the water supply.
solution_steps:
1. Close your water supply valve. Open faucet valve to release pressure build-up in the system.

2. Unscrew filter housing sump from filter cap by hand or using wrench (FXWR1-BL). (Remember to use wrench perpendicularly to the filter housing).

3. Remove old filter cartridge.

4. Remove filter cartridge out of plastic foil and place it inside filter housing sump (pressing against the top of plastic tang to ensure its central location).

5. Lubricate filter housing o-rings, next turn the system 180 degree and lubricate filter cap o-rings.

6. Screw filter housing sump with filter cap using wrench (remember to use the wrench perpendicularly to the filter housing). Use the same procedures for the installation of remaining filter cartridges.

7. Ensure to spread white cosmetic Vaseline (not included in the set) on to O-rings (3 pieces) placed inside filter housing rims.

8. Check if all o-rings and cartridge are positioned correctly.

9. During cartridge installation, follow proper configuration as shown in Table 1 and pay close attention to labels with numeric values placed on the cartridges.

10. WARNING! To seal threaded connections, always use Teflon tape during installation (does not concern threads for plastic and faucet nuts). 

11. Ensure the system is secured from high pressures and rapid pressure changes caused by local water supply systems by installing a pressure regulator on the inlet of the system's water supply. 

12. The system's optimal performance pressure is 3.5.

scenario: FP3-4 system's membrane element is difficult to install due to tight housing.
solution_steps:
1. Shut off water supply valve. Open filter faucet to release pressure from the system.
2. Push in the flange and pull out flexible tubing. Remove UF membrane housing from mounting clips.
3. Unpack new UF membrane out of plastic foil and remove end plugs. Unscrew inlet and outlet connectors from the UF membrane.
4. Remove all layers of old Teflon tape and apply multiple layers of new one. NOTE! Ensure that Teflon tape is winded in the opposite direction to the direction connector will be installed.
5. Connect inlet and outlet connectors to the housing of new UF membrane. NOTE! Do NOT remove elbow connector after the installation has been started. Stopping and removing (unscrewing) the element may result in inadequate connection and water leak.
6. Insert flexible tubing (all the way) into both ends of UF membrane. Check if inlet/outlet tubings are correctly and firmly connected. Make sure the tubing is not bent.
7. Push in membrane housing into mounting clips.
8. Open water supply valve.

scenario: The system leaks after filter cartridge or membrane element replacements.
solution_steps:
1. In case system is leaking, disconnect it from its water supply.
2. Close your water supply valve.
3. Open faucet valve to release pressure build-up in the system.
4. Unscrew filter housing sump from filter cap by hand or using wrench (FXWR1-BL). (Remember to use wrench perpendicularly to the filter housing).
5. Remove old filter cartridge.
6. Remove filter cartridge out of plastic foil and place it inside filter housing sump (pressing against the top of plastic tang to ensure its central location).
7. Lubricate filter housing o-rings, next turn the system 180 degree and lubricate filter cap o-rings.
8. Screw filter housing sump with filter cap using wrench (remember to use the wrench perpendicularly to the filter housing).
9. Use the same procedures for the installation of remaining filter cartridges.

scenario: Water purifier does not connect to the app via Wi-Fi despite following the setup instructions.
solution_steps:
1. Ensure that the BRITA Mypure Max Water Purifier is connected to a power supply and that the power supply is switched ON.

2. Download the BRITA Mypure Max App from the iOS or Android Store.

3. Open the App.

4. Click on "Get Started" to proceed to configuration.

5. Click on "Connect to BRITA Network" to join BRITA network.

6. Choose "Configure Wi-Fi" and select your preferred home Wi-Fi network.

7. Enter password of your selected Wi-Fi network and click on "Save" to connect the Water Purifier to the App.

8. Upon successful configuration, click on "Proceed". Now your Water Purifier is connected to the App and the Wi-Fi symbol in the Water Purifier display will start glowing and show “Connected”.

9. In case of unsuccessful configuration, the display will show ‘Not Connected’. Please repeat steps 5, 6, and 7 to reconfigure.

10. For further clarification please call our Customer Care at 1800 2585 710.

scenario: Difficulty in aligning the filter label and filter base during filter installation, causing improper setup.
solution_steps:
1. Remove the front cover from the Circle as shown. Match this to the arrow on the filter base.
2. Turn the filter(s) to be replaced a quarter-turn counter-clockwise until the unlock arrow on the filter label lines up with the arrow on filter base above it. Pull down to remove.
3. Install the new filter by aligning the arrow indicators on the filter label and filter base above as shown. Push up.
4. Turn a quarter-turn counter-clockwise until the filter stops. The filter base arrow should now point to the “lock” arrow on the filter label.
5. Be sure when replacing the filters that you install the new ones in the correct location by referring to the color coded sticker on the machine and matching to the colored filter labels.

scenario: Water tastes or smells bad, indicating expired filters.
solution_steps:
1. Replace the filters, per the instructions on Page 15.
2. To insert the filters, first line up the arrow on the filter head with the arrow on the filter. NOTE: It is very important to install the filters in the correct order. Simply match the same label colors to the filter head labels. From left-to-right, the proper order is: 1) Sediment filter 2) Pre-Carbon filter 3) Carbon Block filter.
3. With the top and bottom arrows still lined up, insert the top of the filter into the housing and turn to the right, until the filter will not turn any more. The Filter Head arrow should now be lined up with the “dot” on the top of the filter.
4. Repeat the process for the Pre-Carbon filter and Carbon Block filter.

scenario: Water flow is restricted due to filters not being regularly replaced.
solution_steps:
1. Replace the filters as they are not being regularly replaced at the specified times.
2. Write filter replacement date on filter change sticker found on top of each filter.
3. Flush the filters and system with continuous water flow for at least 10 minutes before first time use or after changing any of the filters.
4. Press the button on top of the unit to dispense water (into your sink) and let it run for 10 minutes to flush the system and activate the filters.

scenario: The appliance may not work correctly if the water supply valve is closed.
solution_steps:
1. Turn the valve on the faucet diverter to the side to route the flow of water to the filter unit then turn on cold water.

2. Turn the valve up to use faucet as usual.

3. For the under-counter T-Valve connection type, water should be diverted permanently to the unit once you turn the valve to the “on” position.

4. After turning on water supply, check all connections for any leaks.

5. Wait 5 minutes and check once more for any signs of leaking prior to proceeding to next step.

scenario: It is unsuitable to use the filtered water for aquarium or fishbowl water exchange.
solution_steps:
1. Refer to the manual's caution on page regarding water usage: "Do not use filtered water for the water exchange of an aquarium or a fishbowl."
2. Ensure that you have an alternative source of water that is safe and suitable for aquarium or fishbowl use.
3. Follow the guidelines or recommendations from your aquarium or fishbowl manufacturer or a professional aquarist for the correct water parameters and treatment required for your specific aquatic environment.
4. If unsure about the water quality, consider using a water testing kit to check the parameters such as pH, ammonia, nitrite, and nitrate levels to ensure the safety of the aquatic life.

scenario: Treated water has Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) levels outside the system’s performance guidelines.
solution_steps:
1. Send treated and untreated water samples to a water analysis lab for testing. It is important to test both the treated and untreated water to determine system performance.
2. If the TDS is not within the system's performance guidelines, replace the prefilter, post filter, and RO membrane cartridges.
3. Ensure the water supply to the Reverse Osmosis system is within specifications. Increase water pressure, precondition the water, etc., as needed to conform before doing maintenance on the Reverse Osmosis system.

scenario: Continual water flow to drain and low or no water production due to a plugged drain flow control insert.
solution_steps:
1. Replace the drain flow control insert. See page 21.
2. Periodically check the flow control to be sure the small hole through it is clean and unrestricted.
3. If the flow control requires service, review the exploded view in Fig. 27.
4. Assemble and disassemble as shown in the manual.
5. If the flow control remains in the manifold when the push-in elbow fitting is removed, you will need to remove the drain port’s collet and o-ring to retrieve it.
6. Remove the collet and o-ring from the fitting with a small screwdriver. Do not scratch the internal walls of the collet port. See Figs. 28 & 29.

scenario: Incorrect drain line routing causing leaks at the faucet airgap.
solution_steps:

3. If the drain line is incorrectly connected, adjust the connection following the guidance in the manual. For under sink installations, install the drain adaptor onto your sink’s drain pipe above the P-trap as shown in Figures 8-10.

4. For remote location installations, route the drain tubing to an existing drain in the house, such as a floor drain, laundry tub, standpipe, or sump, as shown in Figures 11 and 12. Ensure there is a 1-1/2" air gap between the end of the hose and the drain point to prevent water from backing up into the system.

5. Consult local plumbing codes to ensure compliance with regulations regarding the type of drain installation used.

6. Verify that the drain tube is cut square and inserted all the way into the red collet fitting on the Reverse Osmosis filter assembly. See Fig. 17 and Fig. 18.

7. Pull on the tubing to ensure it is held firmly in the fitting. 

8. Secure the end of the tubing at the drain point with a bracket (not included) to maintain the air gap. See Fig. 12.
